verses.1:1: And Moab rebelled against Israel after the death of Ahab.
verses.1:2: And Ahaziah fell through the lattice in his upper chamber in Samaria, and became ill. So he sent messengers and said to them, "Go and inquire of Baal-Fly, the god of Ekron, whether I shall recover from this illness of mine." And they went to inquire through him.
verses.1:3: And the angel of the Lord called Elijah the Tishbite, saying, "Arise, go to meet the messengers of Ahaziah king of Samaria, and you shall speak to them, 'Is it because there is no God in Israel that you are going to inquire of Baal-Fly, the god of Ekron? And it is not so,
verses.1:4: for thus says the Lord: The bed upon which you have gone up there—you shall not come down from it, for you shall surely die.'" And Elijah went and spoke to them.
verses.1:5: And the messengers returned to him, and he said to them, "Why is it that you have returned?"
verses.1:6: And they said to him, "A man came up to meet us and said to us, 'Go, return to the king who sent you, and speak to him: Thus says the Lord, Is it because there is no God in Israel that you are going to inquire of Baal-Fly, the god of Ekron? Not so! The bed upon which you have gone up—surely you shall not come down from it, for you shall surely die.'"
verses.1:7: And he spoke to them, "What was the manner of the man who came up to meet you and spoke these words to you?"
verses.1:8: And they said to him, "A hairy man, girded with a leather belt around his waist." And he said, "This is Elijah the Tishbite."
verses.1:9: Then he sent to him a captain of fifty with his fifty men, and he went up to him; and behold, Elijah was sitting on the top of the mountain. And the captain of fifty spoke to him and said, "Man of God, the king has called you; come down!"
verses.1:10: And Elijah answered and said to the captain of fifty, "And if I am a man of God, fire shall come down from heaven and consume you and your fifty men." And fire came down from heaven and consumed him and his fifty men.
verses.1:11: And the king again sent to him another captain of fifty with his fifty men. And the captain of fifty spoke to him and said, "Man of God, thus says the king, 'Come down quickly!'"
verses.1:12: And Elijah answered and spoke to him and said, "If I am a man of God, fire shall come down from heaven and consume you and your fifty men." And fire came down from heaven and consumed him and his fifty men.
verses.1:13: And the king proceeded yet again to send a commander and his fifty men. And the third captain of fifty came and bowed on his knees before Elijah, and pleaded with him and spoke to him and said, "Man of God, let my life and the life of these servants of yours be precious in your sight.
verses.1:14: Behold, fire has come down from heaven and consumed the first two captains of fifty; and now, I pray, let my life be precious in your sight."
verses.1:15: And the angel of the Lord spoke to Elijah and said, "Go down with him; do not be afraid of them." So Elijah arose and went down with him to the king.
verses.1:16: And Elijah spoke to him and said, "Thus says the Lord: 'Why is it that you have sent to inquire of Baal-Fly, the god of Ekron? Not so! The bed upon which you have gone up there—you shall not come down from it, for you shall surely die.'"
verses.1:17: So he died according to the word of the Lord which Elijah had spoken.
verses.1:18: Now the rest of the acts of Ahaziah which he did, behold, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel? And Joram the son of Ahab reigned over Israel in Samaria twelve years, in the eighteenth year of Jehoshaphat king of Judah. And he did evil before the Lord, yet not like his brothers nor like his mother; and he removed the pillars of Baal which his father had made and shattered them. Nevertheless he clung to the sins of the house of Jeroboam, who made Israel sin; he did not depart from them. And the Lord was kindled in wrath against the house of Ahab.
verses.2:1: And it came to pass, when the Lord was about to take up Elijah in a whirlwind as it were into heaven, that Elijah and Elisha went forth from Jericho.
verses.2:2: And Elijah said to Elisha, "Behold now, stay here, for God has sent me as far as Bethel." And Elisha said, "As the Lord lives, and as your soul lives, I will not leave you." So he came to Bethel.
verses.2:3: And the sons of the prophets who were at Bethel came to Elisha and said to him, "Do you know that the Lord is taking your master away from over your head today?" And he said, "I also know it; keep silent."
verses.2:4: Then Elijah said to Elisha, "Stay here, I pray, for the Lord has sent me to Jericho." And he said, "As the Lord lives, and as your soul lives, I will not forsake you." So they came to Jericho.
verses.2:5: And the sons of the prophets who were at Jericho drew near to Elisha and said to him, "Do you know that today the Lord is taking your master away from over your head?" And he said, "Yes, I too know it; keep silent."
verses.2:6: And Elijah said to him, "Stay here, I pray, for the Lord has sent me as far as the Jordan." And Elisha said, "As the Lord lives, and as your soul lives, I will not forsake you." So the two of them went on.
verses.2:7: And fifty men of the sons of the prophets also stood opposite at a distance, while the two of them stood by the Jordan.
verses.2:8: And Elijah took his sheepskin mantle, rolled it up, and struck the water; and the water was divided this way and that, so that the two of them crossed over on dry ground.
verses.2:9: And it came to pass, when they had crossed over, that Elijah said to Elisha, "What shall I do for you before I am taken up from you?" And Elisha said, "Let a double portion of your spirit, I pray, come upon me."
verses.2:10: And Elijah said, "You have asked a hard thing. If you see me being taken up from you, then it shall be so; but if not, it shall not be."
verses.2:11: And it came to pass, as they were going along—walking and talking—that behold, there was a chariot of fire and horses of fire, and it separated the two of them; and Elijah was taken up in a whirlwind as it were into heaven.
verses.2:12: And Elisha saw it, and he cried out, "Father, father, the chariot of Israel and its horseman!" And he did not see him anymore; and he took hold of his own garments and tore them into two pieces.
verses.2:13: And he lifted up the sheepskin mantle of Elijah which had fallen from upon Elisha, and stood by the bank of the Jordan.
verses.2:14: And he took the sheepskin mantle of Elijah, which had fallen from upon him, and struck the water and said, "Where is the God of Elijah, Appho?" And he struck the waters, and they were parted this way and that; and Elisha crossed over.
verses.2:15: And the sons of the prophets and those who were in Jericho saw him from opposite, and said, "The spirit of Elijah rests upon Elisha." And they came to meet him and bowed down to him to the ground.
verses.2:16: And they said to him, "Behold now, there are with your servants fifty men, men of strength. Let them go now and seek your master, lest perhaps the Spirit of the Lord has found him and cast him into the Jordan, or upon one of the mountains, or upon one of the hills." And Elisha said, "You shall not send them."
verses.2:17: Yet they urged him until he was ashamed, and he said, "Send them." So they sent fifty men, and they searched for three days, and did not find him.
verses.2:18: And he was dwelling in Jericho; and Elisha said, "Did I not say to you, 'Do not go'?"
verses.2:19: And the men of the city said to Elisha, "Behold, the habitation of the city is good, as our lord sees, but the waters are bad and the land is barren."
verses.2:20: And Elisha said, "Bring me a new water jar, and put salt in it." And they brought it to him.
verses.2:21: Then Elisha went out to the outlet of the waters and cast salt there, and said, "Thus says the Lord: 'I have healed these waters; from them there shall no longer be death or barrenness.'"
verses.2:22: So the waters have been healed to this day, according to the word of Elisha which he spoke.
verses.2:23: And he went up from there to Bethel; and as he was going up along the road, little boys came out from the city and mocked him, and said to him, "Go up, baldhead, go up!"
verses.2:24: And he turned back behind them and saw them, and cursed them in the name of the Lord. And behold, two bears came out of the woods and tore apart forty-two boys from among them.
verses.2:25: And he went from there to Mount Carmel, and from there he returned to Samaria.
verses.3:1: And Joram the son of Ahab became king in Israel in the eighteenth year of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, and he reigned twelve years.
verses.3:2: And he did evil in the sight of the Lord, yet not like his father and not like his mother; for he removed the pillars of Baal which his father had made.
verses.3:3: Nevertheless he clung to the sin of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who made Israel sin; he did not depart from it.
verses.3:4: Now Mesha king of Moab was a noked, and he rendered to the king of Israel in the rebellion one hundred thousand lambs and one hundred thousand rams with their fleeces.
verses.3:5: And it came to pass, after the death of Ahab, that the king of Moab rebelled against the king of Israel.
verses.3:6: So King Joram went out from Samaria on that day and mustered Israel.
verses.3:7: And he went and sent to Jehoshaphat king of Judah, saying, "The king of Moab has rebelled against me. Will you go with me against Moab to battle?" And he said, "I will go up; as I am, so are you, as my people, so are your people, as my horses, so are your horses."
verses.3:8: And he said, "By which way shall I go up?" And he said, "By the way of the wilderness of Edom."
verses.3:9: So the king of Israel went, and the king of Judah, and the king of Edom, and they marched on a roundabout journey of seven days; and there was no water for the camp nor for the livestock that followed at their feet.
verses.3:10: And the king of Israel said, "Alas! For the Lord has called the three kings passing along to deliver them into the hand of Moab."
verses.3:11: And Jehoshaphat said, "Is there not a prophet of the Lord here, that we may inquire of the Lord by him?" And one of the servants of the king of Israel answered and said, "Here is Elisha the son of Jehoshaphat, who poured water on the hands of Elijah."
verses.3:12: And Jehoshaphat said, "There is a word with him." So the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah and the king of Edom went down to him.
verses.3:13: And Elisha said to the king of Israel, "What have I to do with you? Go to the prophets of your father." And the king of Israel said to him, "No, for the Lord has called the three kings to deliver them into the hands of Moab."
verses.3:14: And Elisha said, "As the Lord of hosts lives, before whom I stand, were it not that I regard the presence of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, I would neither look toward you nor see you.
verses.3:15: And now, bring me a musician." And it came to pass, as the musician played, that the hand of the Lord came upon him.
verses.3:16: And he said, "Thus says the Lord: 'Make this stream-bed full of trenches upon trenches.'
verses.3:17: For thus says the Lord: 'You shall not see wind, and you shall not see rain, yet this stream-bed shall be filled with water, and you shall drink—you, and your herds, and your beasts.
verses.3:18: And this too is a light thing in the sight of the Lord; and I will deliver Moab into your hand.
verses.3:19: And you shall strike every fortified city, and every good tree you shall cut down, and all springs of water you shall stop up, and every good portion of land you shall ruin with stones.'"
verses.3:20: And it came to pass in the morning, as the sacrifice was being offered up, that behold, waters came by the way of Edom, and the land was filled with water.
verses.3:21: And all Moab heard that the kings had come up to fight against them; and they cried out, every one of them girded with a belt, and said, "Alas!" And they took their stand upon the border.
verses.3:22: And they rose early in the morning, and the sun shone upon the waters; and Moab saw the waters opposite them as red as blood.
verses.3:23: And they said, "This is blood of the sword! The kings have fought against one another, and each man has struck his neighbor. And now, to the spoil, Moab!"
verses.3:24: So they came to the camp of Israel; and Israel rose up and struck Moab, and they fled before them. And they entered, advancing and striking Moab.
verses.3:25: And they tore down the cities; and upon every good portion of land each man cast his stone and filled it, and they stopped up every spring, and they cut down every good tree, until they left the stones of the wall torn down. And the slingers surrounded it and struck it.
verses.3:26: And when the king of Moab saw that the battle was too fierce for him, he took with him seven hundred men who drew the sword to break through to the king of Edom; but they could not.
verses.3:27: Then he took his firstborn son, who reigned in his place, and offered him up as a burnt offering upon the wall; and great remorse came upon Israel. So they departed from him and returned to the land.
verses.4:1: And a certain woman from the sons of the prophets cried out to Elisha, saying, "Your servant my husband has died, and you know that he was a servant who feared the Lord; and the creditor has come to take my two sons for himself as servants."
verses.4:2: And Elisha said, "What shall I do for you? What do you have in the house?" And she said, "Your maidservant has nothing at all, except oil with which I may anoint myself."
verses.4:3: And he said to her, "Go, ask for vessels for yourself outside from all the neighbors, empty vessels; do not ask for only a few.
verses.4:4: And you shall enter and shut the door behind you and behind your sons, and you shall pour out into these vessels; and whatever is filled you shall set aside."
verses.4:5: So she departed from him and shut the door behind herself and behind her sons; they brought them near to her, and she kept pouring until the vessels were filled.
verses.4:6: And she said to her sons, "Bring yet another vessel to me." And they said to her, "There is no longer a vessel." And the oil ceased.
verses.4:7: And she came and told the man of God. And Elisha said, "Go and sell the oil, and you shall pay your interest, and you and your sons shall live on the remaining oil."
verses.4:8: Now it came to pass one day that Elisha crossed over to Shunem, and there was a prominent woman there, and she prevailed upon him to eat bread. And it came to pass that as often as he went in, he turned aside to eat there.
verses.4:9: And the woman said to her husband, "Behold now, I know that this is a holy man of God who continually passes by us.
verses.4:10: Let us make for him now an upper chamber, a small place, and let us put there for him a bed and a table and a chair and a lampstand; and it shall be, whenever he comes in to us, that he will turn aside there."
verses.4:11: And there came a day when he entered there, and he turned aside into the upper chamber and slept there.
verses.4:12: And he said to Gehazi his servant, "Call this Shunammite woman for me." And he called her, and she stood before him.
verses.4:13: And he said to him, "Say now to her, 'Behold, you have set aside for us all this possession; what must be done for you? Do you have a word for the king, or for the commander of the host?'" And she said, "I dwell in the midst of the people."
verses.4:14: And he said, "What must be done for her?" And Gehazi his servant said, "Indeed, she has no son, and her husband is an old man."
verses.4:15: And he called her, and she stood by the door.
verses.4:16: And Elisha said to her, "At this season, as the hour lives, you shall be embracing a son." And she said, "No, my lord, do not deceive your maidservant."
verses.4:17: And the woman conceived and bore a son at this season, as the hour lives, just as Elisha had spoken to her.
verses.4:18: And the child grew; and it came to pass, when he went out to his father, to the reapers,
verses.4:19: that he said to his father, "My head, my head!" And he said to the servant, "Carry him to his mother."
verses.4:20: And he lay upon her knees until noon, and died.
verses.4:21: And she carried him up and laid him upon the bed of the man of God, and shut the door behind him, and went out.
verses.4:22: And she called her husband and said, "Send me now one of the servants and one of the donkeys, and I will run to the man of God and return."
verses.4:23: And he said, "Why are you going to him today? It is neither new moon nor Sabbath." And she said, "Peace."
verses.4:24: And she saddled the donkey and said to her servant, "Drive on and go; do not hold back the riding for me, unless I tell you.
verses.4:25: Go and proceed, and you shall come to the man of God at Mount Carmel." And it came to pass, when Elisha saw her coming, that he said to Gehazi his servant, "Behold now, that Shunammite woman!
verses.4:26: Run now to meet her, and you shall say, 'Is it peace with you? Is it peace with your husband? Is it peace with the child?'" And she said, "Peace."
verses.4:27: And she came to Elisha at the mountain and took hold of his feet; and Gehazi drew near to push her away. And Elisha said, "Leave her alone, for her soul is deeply distressed within her, and the Lord has hidden it from me and from you, and has not told me."
verses.4:28: And she said, "Did I ask a son from my lord? Did I not say, 'You shall not deceive me'?"
verses.4:29: And Elisha said to Gehazi, "Gird up your loins, and take my staff in your hand, and go; for if you meet a man, you shall not bless him, and if a man blesses you, you shall not answer him; and you shall lay my staff upon the face of the child."
verses.4:30: And the mother of the child said, "As the Lord lives, and as your soul lives, I will not leave you." So Elisha arose and went after her.
verses.4:31: And Gehazi passed on before her and laid the staff upon the face of the child, and there was no voice and there was no hearing. So he returned to meet him and told him, saying, "The child has not awakened."
verses.4:32: And Elisha entered into the house, and behold, the child was dead, laid upon his bed.
verses.4:33: And Elisha entered into the house and shut the door behind the two of them, and prayed to the Lord.
verses.4:34: And he went up and lay upon the child, and put his mouth upon his mouth, and his eyes upon his eyes, and his hands upon his hands, and he bent over him; and the flesh of the child grew warm.
verses.4:35: And he returned and walked back and forth in the house, and went up and bowed over the child up to seven times; and the child opened his eyes.
verses.4:36: And Elisha cried out to Gehazi and said, "Call this Shunammite woman." And he called her, and she came in to him. And Elisha said, "Take your son."
verses.4:37: And the woman came in and fell at his feet and bowed down to the ground, and she took her son and went out.
verses.4:38: And Elisha returned to Gilgal; and the famine was in the land, and the sons of the prophets were sitting before him. And Elisha said to his servant, "Set on the pot, and boil stew for the sons of the prophets."
verses.4:39: And he went out into the field to gather arioth; and he found a vine in the field, and gathered from it wild gourds, his garment full, and cast them into the pot of stew, for they did not know. And he poured out for the men to eat.
verses.4:40: And it came to pass, as they were eating of the stew, that behold, they cried out and said, "There is death in the pot, O man of God!" And they were not able to eat.
verses.4:41: And he said, "Take flour and cast it into the pot." And Elisha said to Gehazi the servant, "Pour out for the people, and let them eat." And there was no longer any harmful thing there in the pot.
verses.4:42: And a man came through from Beth-sarisa and brought to the man of God from the firstfruits twenty barley loaves and fig cakes. And he said, "Give to the people, and let them eat."
verses.4:43: And his attendant said, "What? Shall I set this before one hundred men?" And he said, "Give to the people, and let them eat; for thus says the Lord, 'They shall eat and have some left over.'"
verses.4:44: And they ate and had some left over, according to the word of the Lord.
verses.5:1: Now Naaman, the commander of the host of Syria, was a great man before his lord and admired in person, because by him the Lord had given deliverance to Syria; and the man was mighty in strength, a leper.
verses.5:2: And Syria went out in raiding bands and took captive from the land of Israel a little maiden, and she was before the wife of Naaman.
verses.5:3: And she said to her mistress, "Oh, that my lord were before the prophet of God who is in Samaria! Then he would restore him from his leprosy."
verses.5:4: And she went in and told her lord and said, "Thus and thus spoke the maiden who is from the land of Israel."
verses.5:5: And the king of Syria said to Naaman, "Go, enter in, and I will send a letter to the king of Israel." So he departed and took in his hand ten talents of silver, and six thousand pieces of gold, and ten changes of garments.
verses.5:6: And he brought the letter to the king of Israel, saying, "And now, when this letter comes to you, behold, I have sent Naaman my servant to you, and you shall restore him from his leprosy."
verses.5:7: And it came to pass, when the king of Israel read the letter, that he tore his garments and said, "Am I God, to put to death and to make alive, that this man sends to me to restore a man from his leprosy? Only know now and see that this man is seeking a pretext against me."
verses.5:8: And it came to pass, when Elisha heard that the king of Israel had torn his garments, that he sent to the king of Israel, saying, "Why have you torn your garments? Let Naaman come now to me, and let him know that there is a prophet in Israel."
verses.5:9: So Naaman came with horse and chariot, and stood at the door of the house of Elisha.
verses.5:10: And Elisha sent a messenger to him, saying, "Go and wash seven times in the Jordan, and your flesh shall be restored to you, and you shall be cleansed."
verses.5:11: And Naaman became angry, and departed and said, "Behold, I said, 'He will surely come out to me, and call upon the name of his God, and lay his hand upon the place, and remove the leprosy.'
verses.5:12: Are not Abana and Apharpha, the rivers of Damascus, better than all the waters of Israel? May I not go and wash in them and be cleansed?" And he turned aside and departed in wrath.
verses.5:13: And his servants drew near and spoke to him, "If the prophet had spoken a great word to you, would you not do it? And now when he said to you, 'Wash and be cleansed'?"
verses.5:14: So Naaman went down and dipped himself in the Jordan seven times, according to the word of Elisha; and his flesh was restored like the flesh of a little child, and he was cleansed.
verses.5:15: And he returned to Elisha, he and all his company, and came and stood and said, "Behold, I know that there is no God in all the earth except in Israel; and now, take the blessing from your servant."
verses.5:16: And Elisha said, "As the Lord lives, before whom I stand, I will not take it." And he urged him to take it, but he refused.
verses.5:17: And Naaman said, "And if not, let there be given now to your servant a gomer, pairs of mules; for your servant will no longer offer burnt offering and sacrifice to other gods, except to the Lord.
verses.5:18: In this thing also may the Lord pardon your servant: when my lord goes into the house of Rimmon to bow down there, and he leans upon my hand, and I bow down in the house of Rimmon when he bows down in the house of Rimmon, may the Lord indeed pardon your servant in this matter."
verses.5:19: And Elisha said to Naaman, "Go in peace." And he departed from him for a debratha of the land.
verses.5:20: And Gehazi, the servant of Elisha, said, "Behold, my lord has spared this Naaman the Syrian, in not receiving from his hand what he brought; as the Lord lives, I will surely run after him and take something from him."
verses.5:21: So Gehazi pursued after Naaman; and Naaman saw him running after him, and turned back from the chariot to meet him.
verses.5:22: And he said, "Peace. My lord has sent me, saying, 'Behold, just now two young men from Mount Ephraim, of the sons of the prophets, have come to me; give them now a talent of silver and two changes of garments.'"
verses.5:23: And Naaman said, "Take two talents of silver." And he took them in two bags, and two changes of garments; and he laid them upon two of his servants, and they carried them before him.
verses.5:24: And they came to the dark place, and he took them from their hands and stored them in the house, and he sent the men away.
verses.5:25: And he himself went in and stood beside his lord. And Elisha said to him, "From where have you come, Gehazi?" And Gehazi said, "Your servant has not gone here or there."
verses.5:26: And Elisha said to him, "Did not my heart go with you when the man turned back from the chariot to meet you? And now you have received the silver, and now you have received the garments, and olive groves and vineyards, and sheep and oxen, and menservants and maidservants;
verses.5:27: and the leprosy of Naaman shall cling to you and to your seed forever." And he went out from his presence leprous as snow.
verses.6:1: And the sons of the prophets said to Elisha, "Behold now, the place in which we dwell before you is too narrow for us.
verses.6:2: Let us go now to the Jordan, and let us take from there each man one beam, and let us prepare for ourselves there to dwell there." And he said, "Go."
verses.6:3: And one of them said, "Kindly come with your servants." And he said, "I will go."
verses.6:4: So he went with them, and they came to the Jordan and were cutting down the trees.
verses.6:5: And behold, as one of them was felling the beam, the iron head fell out into the water; and he cried out, "Alas, master! And it is hidden!"
verses.6:6: And the man of God said, "Where did it fall?" And he showed him the place; and he broke off a piece of wood and cast it there, and the iron head floated.
verses.6:7: And he said, "Lift it up for yourself." So he stretched out his hand and took it.
verses.6:8: Now the king of Syria was making war against Israel; and he took counsel with his servants, saying, "In such and such a place, Elimoni, I will encamp."
verses.6:9: And Elisha sent to the king of Israel, saying, "Beware that you do not pass through this place, for there Syria is hidden."
verses.6:10: And the king of Israel sent to the place of which Elisha had told him, and he kept guard from there not once nor twice.
verses.6:11: And the soul of the king of Syria was greatly agitated concerning this matter; and he called his servants and said to them, "Will you not tell me who betrays me to the king of Israel?"
verses.6:12: And one of his servants said, "No, my lord, O king; for Elisha, the prophet who is in Israel, declares to the king of Israel all the words that you speak in the inner room of your bedchamber."
verses.6:13: And he said, "Go and see where this man is, and I will send and take him." And they told him, saying, "Behold, he is in Dothan."
verses.6:14: So he sent there horses and chariots and a great force, and they came by night and surrounded the city.
verses.6:15: And the attendant of Elisha rose early in the morning and went out; and behold, a force was surrounding the city, both horses and chariots. And the young servant said to him, "Alas, master! What shall we do?"
verses.6:16: And Elisha said, "Do not fear, for those who are with us are more than those who are with them."
verses.6:17: And Elisha prayed and said, "O Lord, open the eyes of the young servant, that he may see." And the Lord opened his eyes, and he saw; and behold, the mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire all around Elisha.
verses.6:18: And they came down to him; and he prayed to the Lord and said, "Strike now this nation with blindness." And He struck them with blindness according to the word of Elisha.
verses.6:19: And Elisha said to them, "This is not the city, nor is this the way; come after me, and I will lead you to the man whom you seek." And he led them away to Samaria.
verses.6:20: And it came to pass, when they had entered into Samaria, that Elisha said, "Open now, O Lord, their eyes, that they may see." And He opened their eyes, and they saw; and behold, they were in the midst of Samaria.
verses.6:21: And the king of Israel said, when he saw them, "Shall I surely strike them down, father?"
verses.6:22: And he said, "You shall not strike them down, unless you strike those whom you have taken captive with your sword and your bow. Set bread and water before them, that they may eat and drink, and let them depart to their master."
verses.6:23: So he set before them a great feast, and they ate and drank; and he sent them away to their master. And the raiding bands of Syria no longer came into the land of Israel.
verses.6:24: And it came to pass after these things that the son of Hader, king of Syria, gathered all his army and went up, and they besieged Samaria.
verses.6:25: And there was a great famine in Samaria; and behold, they besieged it until a donkey's head was sold for fifty pieces of silver, and a fourth of a kab of doves' dung for five pieces of silver.
verses.6:26: And the king of Israel was passing along on the wall, and a woman cried out to him, saying, "Save me, O lord king!"
verses.6:27: And he said to her, "May the Lord not save you! From where shall I save you? From the threshing floor, or from the winepress?"
verses.6:28: And the king said to her, "What is the matter with you?" And the woman said, "This woman said to me, 'Give your son, and we will eat him today; and my son, and we will eat him tomorrow.'
verses.6:29: So we boiled my son and ate him; and I said to her on the second day, 'Give your son, that we may eat him,' but she has hidden her son."
verses.6:30: And it came to pass, when the king heard the words of the woman, that he tore his garments; and he was passing along on the wall, and the people saw the sackcloth on his flesh underneath.
verses.6:31: And he said, "May God do so to me, and more also, if the head of Elisha shall remain on him today."
verses.6:32: Now Elisha was sitting in his house, and the elders were sitting with him. And the king had sent a man from before his presence; and before the messenger came to him, he said to the elders, "Did you know that the son of the murderer has sent to take away my head? Look, when the messenger comes, shut the door and press him back at the door. Is not the sound of his master's feet behind him?"
verses.6:33: While he was still speaking with them, behold, a messenger came down to him and said, "Behold, this calamity is from the Lord; why should I wait for the Lord any longer?"
verses.7:1: And Elisha said, "Hear the word of the Lord! Thus says the Lord: 'About this time tomorrow, a measure of fine flour shall be sold for a shekel in the gates of Samaria.'"
verses.7:2: And the officer on whose hand the king leaned answered Elisha and said, "Behold, the Lord will make floodgates in heaven; could this thing be?" And Elisha said, "Behold, you shall see it with your eyes, yet you shall not eat of it."
verses.7:3: Now there were four leprous men by the entrance of the city; and one man said to his neighbor, "Why do we sit here until we die?
verses.7:4: If we say, 'Let us enter into the city,' the famine is in the city, and we shall die there; and if we sit here, we shall also die. Now therefore, come, and let us go over to the camp of Syria: if they spare our lives, we shall live; and if they put us to death, we shall die."
verses.7:5: And they arose in the darkness to enter into the camp of Syria; and they came into the midst of the camp of Syria, and behold, there was no man there.
verses.7:6: For the Lord had caused the camp of Syria to hear the sound of chariots and the sound of horses, even the sound of a great army; and one man said to his brother, "Now the king of Israel has hired against us the kings of the Hittites and the kings of Egypt to come against us!"
verses.7:7: So they arose and fled in the darkness, and abandoned their tents and their horses and their donkeys in the camp just as it was, and fled for their lives.
verses.7:8: And these lepers entered as far as the outskirts of the camp, and went into one tent and ate and drank, and carried away from there silver and gold and clothing; and they went away and returned from there, and entered into another tent, and took from there, and went away and hid them.
verses.7:9: Then one man said to his neighbor, "We should not act thus! This day is a day of good tidings, yet we keep silent; and if we wait until the light of the morning, we shall find iniquity. Now therefore, come, and let us go in and report to the house of the king."
verses.7:10: So they came and cried out to the gate of the city, and reported to them, saying, "We entered into the camp of Syria, and behold, there is no man there, nor the voice of a man, but only horses tied and donkeys, and their tents just as they are."
verses.7:11: And the gatekeepers cried out and reported it to the house of the king within.
verses.7:12: And the king arose in the night and said to his servants, "I will now tell you what Syria has done to us. They know that we are hungry, so they have gone out of the camp and hidden themselves in the field, saying, 'They will come out of the city, and we shall take them alive and enter into the city.'"
verses.7:13: And one of his servants answered and said, "Let them now take five of the remaining horses that have been left here—behold, they are like all the multitude of Israel that is perishing—and we will send them there and see."
verses.7:14: So they took two riders of horses, and the king of Israel sent them after the king of Syria, saying, "Go and see."
verses.7:15: And they went after them as far as the Jordan; and behold, all the way was full of garments and equipment that Syria had cast away in their terror. And the messengers returned and reported to the king.
verses.7:16: Then the people went out and plundered the camp of Syria; and a measure of fine flour was sold for a shekel, according to the word of the Lord, and two measures of barley for a shekel.
verses.7:17: Now the king had appointed the officer on whose hand the king leaned over the gate; and the people trampled him in the gate, and he died, just as the man of God had spoken, who spoke when the messenger came down to him.
verses.7:18: And it came to pass just as Elisha had spoken to the king, saying, "Two measures of barley for a shekel, and a measure of fine flour for a shekel, and it shall be about this time tomorrow in the gate of Samaria."
verses.7:19: And the officer had answered Elisha and said, "Behold, the Lord makes floodgates in heaven—this thing shall by no means be!" And Elisha had said, "Behold, you shall see it with your eyes, yet you shall by no means eat of it."
verses.7:20: And so it came to pass, for the people trampled him in the gate, and he died.
verses.8:1: Now Elisha spoke to the woman whose son he had restored to life, saying, "Arise and go, you and your household, and sojourn wherever you may sojourn; for the Lord has called a famine upon the land, and indeed it has come upon the land for seven years."
verses.8:2: So the woman arose and did according to the word of Elisha; and she and her household went and sojourned in the land of the Philistines for seven years.
verses.8:3: And it came to pass, after the end of the seven years, that the woman returned from the land of the Philistines into the city; and she came to cry out to the king concerning her house and concerning her fields.
verses.8:4: Now the king was speaking to Gehazi, the servant of Elisha the man of God, saying, "Tell me, please, all the great things that Elisha has done."
verses.8:5: And it came to pass, as he was recounting to the king how he had restored a dead son to life, that behold, the woman whose son Elisha had restored to life was crying out to the king concerning her house and concerning her fields. And Gehazi said, "My lord, O king, this is the woman, and this is her son whom Elisha restored to life."
verses.8:6: And the king asked the woman, and she recounted it to him. So the king assigned a certain eunuch to her, saying, "Restore all her produce of the field, from the day that she left the land until now."
verses.8:7: Then Elisha came to Damascus, and the son of Hader, king of Syria, was sick. And they reported to him, saying, "The man of God has come even here."
verses.8:8: And the king said to Hazael, "Take a present in your hand, and go to meet the man of God, and inquire of the Lord through him, saying, 'Shall I recover from this sickness of mine?'"
verses.8:9: So Hazael went to meet him, and took a present in his hand, even all the good things of Damascus, the burden of forty camels, as gifts. And he came and stood before him, and said to Elisha, "Your son, the son of Hader, king of Syria, has sent me to you to inquire, saying, 'Shall I recover from this sickness of mine?'"
verses.8:10: And Elisha said, "Go, say, 'You shall surely live'; yet the Lord has shown me that you shall surely die."
verses.8:11: And he stood before his face, and fixed his countenance until he was ashamed; and the man of God wept.
verses.8:12: And Hazael said, "Why does my lord weep?" And he said, "Because I know all the evil that you will do to the children of Israel: their strongholds you will set on fire, and their chosen men you will slay with the sword, and their little ones you will dash in pieces, and their women with child you will rip open."
verses.8:13: And Hazael said, "Who is your servant, a dead dog, that he should do this thing?" And Elisha said, "The Lord has shown me you reigning over Israel."
verses.8:14: So he departed from Elisha and went in to his master, who said to him, "What did Elisha say to you?" And he said, "He told me, 'You shall surely live.'"
verses.8:15: And it came to pass on the next day that he took the coverlet, and dipped it in water, and spread it over his face, so that he died. And Hazael reigned in his place.
verses.8:16: In the fifth year of Joram the son of Ahab, king of Israel, while Jehoshaphat was king of Judah, Joram the son of Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, began to reign.
verses.8:17: He was thirty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned forty years in Jerusalem.
verses.8:18: And he walked in the way of the kings of Israel, just as the house of Ahab had done, for the daughter of Ahab was his wife; and he did evil in the sight of the Lord.
verses.8:19: Yet the Lord was not willing to destroy Judah, for the sake of David His servant, as He had promised to give him a lamp all the days.
verses.8:20: In his days Edom revolted from under the hand of Judah, and they made a king to reign over themselves.
verses.8:21: So Joram went up to Seior, and all the chariots with him. And it came to pass, when he arose, that he struck down Edom, who had surrounded him, and the commanders of the chariots; and the people fled to their tents.
verses.8:22: Yet Edom has revolted from under the hand of Judah to this day. Then Senna revolted at that same time.
verses.8:23: Now the rest of the acts of Joram, and all that he did, behold, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
verses.8:24: So Joram slept with his fathers, and was buried with his fathers in the city of David his father. And Ahaziah his son reigned in his place.
verses.8:25: In the twelfth year of Joram the son of Ahab, king of Israel, Ahaziah the son of Joram began to reign.
verses.8:26: Ahaziah was twenty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned one year in Israel. And his mother's name was Athaliah, the daughter of Omri, king of Israel.
verses.8:27: And he walked in the way of the house of Ahab, and did evil in the sight of the Lord, just as the house of Ahab had done.
verses.8:28: And he went with Joram the son of Ahab to war against Hazael, king of the foreigners, at Ramoth Gilead; and the Syrians struck Joram.
verses.8:29: Then King Joram returned to be healed in Israel from the wounds with which they had struck him at Ramoth, when he fought against Hazael, king of Syria. And Ahaziah the son of Joram went down to see Joram the son of Ahab in Israel, because he was sick.
verses.9:1: Now Elisha the prophet called one of the sons of the prophets, and said to him, "Gird up your loins, and take this flask of oil in your hand, and go to Ramoth Gilead.
verses.9:2: And when you arrive there, look there for Jehu the son of Jehoshaphat, the son of Nimshi, and go in and make him rise up from among his brethren, and bring him into an inner chamber.
verses.9:3: Then take the flask of oil, and pour it on his head, and say, 'Thus says the Lord: I have anointed you king over Israel.' Then open the door and flee, and do not linger."
verses.9:4: So the young man, the prophet, went to Ramoth Gilead.
verses.9:5: And when he came, behold, the commanders of the army were sitting there; and he said, "I have a word for you, O commander." And Jehu said, "For which one of us all?" And he said, "For you, O commander."
verses.9:6: Then he arose and went into the house. And he poured the oil on his head, and said to him, "Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: 'I have anointed you king over the people of the Lord, over Israel.
verses.9:7: And you shall utterly destroy the house of Ahab your master from before your face, and you shall avenge the blood of My servants the prophets, and the blood of all the servants of the Lord, at the hand of Jezebel,
verses.9:8: and at the hand of all the house of Ahab; and you shall utterly destroy from the house of Ahab every male, both confined and forsaken in Israel.
verses.9:9: And I will make the house of Ahab like the house of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, and like the house of Baasha the son of Ahijah.
verses.9:10: And the dogs shall devour Jezebel in the portion of Israel, and there shall be none to bury her.'" Then he opened the door and fled.
verses.9:11: Then Jehu came out to the servants of his master, and they said to him, "Is it peace? Why did this madman come in to you?" And he said to them, "You know the man and his babbling."
verses.9:12: And one said, "False! Tell us now." And Jehu said to them, "Thus and thus he spoke to me, saying"—and he said—"Thus says the Lord: 'I have anointed you king over Israel.'"
verses.9:13: And when they heard it, they hastened, and each man took his garment and placed it beneath him on the top of the steps; and they blew the horn and proclaimed, "Jehu is king!"
verses.9:14: So Jehu the son of Jehoshaphat, the son of Nimshi, conspired against Joram. Now Joram himself had been keeping watch at Ramoth Gilead, he and all Israel, because of Hazael, king of Syria.
verses.9:15: But King Joram had returned to be healed in Israel from the wounds with which the Syrians had struck him when they fought against Hazael, king of Syria. And Jehu said, "If your soul is with me, let no fugitive go forth from the city to go and report it in Israel."
verses.9:16: So Jehu rode and went, and came down to Israel; for Joram, king of Israel, was being healed in Israel from the arrow wounds with which the Arameans had shot him at Ramoth in the war against Hazael, king of Syria, because he was mighty and a man of valor. And Ahaziah, king of Judah, had come down to see Joram.
verses.9:17: Now the watchman went up upon the tower of Israel, and saw the dust cloud of Jehu as he approached, and said, "I see a cloud of dust." And Joram said, "Take a horseman and send him before them, and let him say, 'Is it peace?'"
verses.9:18: So the horseman went to meet them, and said, "Thus says the king: 'Is it peace?'" And Jehu said, "What have you to do with peace? Turn behind me." And the watchman reported, saying, "The messenger reached them, and has not returned."
verses.9:19: Then he sent a second horseman, and he came to him and said, "Thus says the king: 'Is it peace?'" And Jehu said, "What have you to do with peace? Turn behind me."
verses.9:20: And the watchman reported, saying, "He reached them, and has not returned; and the driver was driving Jehu the son of Nimshi, for it was in a frenzy."
verses.9:21: Then Joram said, "Harness!" And he harnessed a chariot. So Joram, king of Israel, and Ahaziah, king of Judah, went out, each man in his chariot; and they went out to meet Jehu, and found him in the portion of Naboth the Israelite.
verses.9:22: And it came to pass, when Joram saw Jehu, that he said, "Is it peace, Jehu?" And Jehu said, "What peace, while the harlotries of Jezebel your mother and her many sorceries still remain?"
verses.9:23: Then Joram turned his hands around and fled, and said to Ahaziah, "Treachery, Ahaziah!"
verses.9:24: Now Jehu filled his hand with the bow and struck Joram between his arms; and his arrow went out through his heart, and he sank down upon his knees.
verses.9:25: Then he said to Bidkar his captain, "Cast him into the portion of the field of Naboth the Israelite; for I remember how I and you were riding in pairs behind Ahab his father, when the Lord took up this burden against him:
verses.9:26: 'Surely I saw yesterday the blood of Naboth and the blood of his sons, says the Lord; and I will repay him in this portion, says the Lord.' Now therefore, take him up now and cast him into the portion, according to the word of the Lord."
verses.9:27: When Ahaziah, king of Judah, saw this, he fled by the way of Bethan. And Jehu pursued after him and said, "Him also!" And he struck him at the chariot at the ascent of Gai, which is Ibleam; and he fled to Megiddo, and died there.
verses.9:28: And his servants placed him upon the chariot and brought him to Jerusalem, and buried him in his tomb in the city of David.
verses.9:29: And in the eleventh year of Joram, king of Israel, Ahaziah had begun to reign over Judah.
verses.9:30: Now Jehu came to Israel; and Jezebel heard of it, and she painted her eyes and adorned her head, and looked out through the window.
verses.9:31: And as Jehu entered into the city, she said, "Is it peace, Zimri, murderer of his master?"
verses.9:32: And he lifted up his face toward the window and saw her, and said, "Who are you? Come down with me!" And two eunuchs looked down to him.
verses.9:33: And he said, "Cast her down!" So they cast her down; and some of her blood was spattered upon the wall and upon the horses, and they trampled her underfoot.
verses.9:34: And he went in and ate and drank, and said, "See now to this accursed woman and bury her, for she is a king's daughter."
verses.9:35: So they went to bury her, but they found nothing of her except the skull, and the feet, and the palms of the hands.
verses.9:36: Therefore they returned and told him. And he said, "This is the word of the Lord, which He spoke by the hand of Elijah the Tishbite, saying, 'In the portion of Israel the dogs shall devour the flesh of Jezebel;
verses.9:37: and the carcass of Jezebel shall be as refuse upon the face of the field in the portion of Israel, so that they shall not say, Jezebel.'"
verses.10:1: Now Ahab had seventy sons in Samaria. And Jehu wrote a letter and sent it to Samaria, to the rulers of Samaria, and to the elders, and to the guardians of Ahab, saying,
verses.10:2: "And now, as soon as this letter comes to you, since your master's sons are with you, and with you are the chariot and horses, and fortified cities, and armor,
verses.10:3: look out for the good and upright one among your master's sons, and set him upon his father's throne, and fight for the house of your master."
verses.10:4: And they were exceedingly afraid, and said, "Behold, the two kings did not stand before him; and how shall we stand?"
verses.10:5: And those who were over the house, and those who were over the city, and the elders, and the guardians sent to Jehu, saying, "We are your servants, and whatever you say to us we will do. We will not make any man king; what is good in your eyes we will do."
verses.10:6: Then he wrote a second letter to them, saying, "If you are mine, and if you listen to my voice, take the heads of the men, the sons of your master, and bring them to me about this time tomorrow to Israel." Now the sons of the king were seventy men; these great men of the city were rearing them.
verses.10:7: And it came to pass, when the letter came to them, that they took the sons of the king and slaughtered them, seventy men; and they placed their heads in baskets and sent them to him to Israel.
verses.10:8: And the messenger came and reported, saying, "I have brought the heads of the king's sons." And he said, "Lay them in two heaps by the entrance of the city gate until morning."
verses.10:9: And it came to pass in the morning that he went out and stood, and said to all the people, "You are righteous. Behold, I myself conspired against my master and slew him; yet who has struck down all these?
verses.10:10: See then, that nothing of the word of the Lord shall fall to the earth, which the Lord spoke concerning the house of Ahab; for the Lord has done all that He spoke by the hand of His servant Elijah."
verses.10:11: So Jehu struck down all who remained in the house of Ahab in Israel, and all his great men, and his close acquaintances, and his priests, until he left them no remnant.
verses.10:12: And he arose and went toward Samaria. As he was at Beth-eked of the shepherds on the way,
verses.10:13: Jehu met the brethren of Ahaziah king of Judah, and said, "Who are you?" And they said, "We are the brethren of Ahaziah, and we have come down for the welfare of the sons of the king and the sons of the ruling queen."
verses.10:14: And he said, "Take them alive!" And they slaughtered them at Beth-eked, forty-two men; he did not leave a man of them.
verses.10:15: And he departed from there and received Jonadab the son of Rechab coming to meet him, and he blessed him. And Jehu said to him, "Is your heart right with my heart, as my heart is with your heart?" And Jonadab said, "It is." And Jehu said, "And if it is, give your hand." And he gave his hand, and he brought him up to himself into the chariot.
verses.10:16: And he said to him, "Come with me, and see my zeal for the Lord." And he seated him in his chariot.
verses.10:17: And he entered Samaria, and struck down all who remained of Ahab in Samaria until he had destroyed him, according to the word of the Lord which He spoke to Elijah.
verses.10:18: And Jehu was zealous for all the people, and said to them, "Ahab served Baal a little; Jehu will serve him much.
verses.10:19: And now, all you prophets of Baal, call to me all his servants and his priests; let no man be missing, for I have a great sacrifice to Baal; everyone who is missing shall not live." Now Jehu did this in craftiness, that he might destroy the servants of Baal.
verses.10:20: And Jehu said, "Sanctify a sacred festival to Baal." And he proclaimed it.
verses.10:21: And Jehu sent throughout all Israel, saying, "And now, all his servants and all his priests and all his prophets, let no one be left behind, for I am making a great sacrifice; whoever is left behind shall not live." And all the servants of Baal came, and all his priests, and all his prophets; there was not a man left who did not come. And they entered the house of Baal, and the house of Baal was filled from mouth to mouth.
verses.10:22: And he said to the one who was over the house of mesthaal, "Bring out a garment for all the servants of Baal." And the keeper of the robes brought it out to them.
verses.10:23: Then Jehu and Jonadab the son of Rechab entered the house of Baal, and he said to the servants of Baal, "Search and see whether any of the servants of the Lord are with you, for there must be none except the servants of Baal alone."
verses.10:24: And he went in to offer the sacrifices and the burnt offerings. Now Jehu had appointed for himself eighty men outside, and said, "If any man escapes from the men whom I bring into your hands, his life shall be for his life."
verses.10:25: And it came to pass, as soon as he had finished offering the burnt offering, that Jehu said to the guards and to the officers, "Go in and strike them down; let no man come out from among them!" And they struck them down with the edge of the sword; and the guards and the officers cast them out, and went as far as the city of the house of Baal.
verses.10:26: And they brought out the robe of Baal and burned it.
verses.10:27: And they tore down the pillars of Baal, and he struck it down into latrines until this day.
verses.10:28: Thus Jehu destroyed Baal out of Israel.
verses.10:29: Nevertheless, from the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin, Jehu did not depart from before them—the golden heifers that were in Bethel and in Dan.
verses.10:30: And the Lord said to Jehu, "Because you have done well in doing what is upright in My eyes, and have done to the house of Ahab according to all that was in My heart, your sons to the fourth generation shall sit upon the throne of Israel."
verses.10:31: Yet Jehu did not take care to walk in the law of the Lord God of Israel with all his heart; he did not depart from the sins of Jeroboam, who caused Israel to sin.
verses.10:32: In those days the Lord began to cut off parts of Israel; and Hazael struck them down throughout all the territory of Israel,
verses.10:33: from the Jordan toward the rising of the sun, all Gilead—of the Gadites, and of Reuben, and of Manasseh—from Aroer, which is upon the bank of the brook Arnon, both Gilead and Bashan.
verses.10:34: Now the rest of the acts of Jehu, and all that he did, and all his might, and the engagements which he joined, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
verses.10:35: And Jehu slept with his fathers, and they buried him in Samaria; and Jehoahaz his son reigned in his place.
verses.10:36: And the days that Jehu reigned over Israel were twenty-eight years in Samaria.
verses.11:1: And Athaliah the mother of Ahaziah saw that her son was dead, and she destroyed all the seed of the kingdom.
verses.11:2: But Jehosheba, the daughter of King Joram, sister of Ahaziah, took Joash the son of her brother, and stole him away from the midst of the king's sons who were being put to death, him and his nurse, into the chamber of beds; and she hid him from the presence of Athaliah, and he was not put to death.
verses.11:3: And he was with her, hidden in the house for six years, while Athaliah was reigning over the land.
verses.11:4: And in the seventh year Jehoiada sent and took the captains of hundreds, the Chorri and the Rasin, and brought them to himself into the house of the Lord; and he made a covenant of the Lord with them and put them under oath. And Jehoiada showed them the king's son,
verses.11:5: and commanded them, saying, "This is the thing that you shall do: a third of you shall come in on the Sabbath, and you shall keep the watch of the king's house in the gateway,
verses.11:6: and a third at the gate of the ways, and a third at the gate behind the guards; and you shall keep the watch of the house.
verses.11:7: And two companies among you, everyone who goes out on the Sabbath, shall keep the watch of the house of the Lord by the king.
verses.11:8: And surround the king all around, each man with his weapon in his hand; and whoever enters into the aedoth shall die." And he was with the king when he went out and when he came in.
verses.11:9: And the captains of hundreds did all that Jehoiada the wise commanded; and each man took his men, even those who came in on the Sabbath, and came to Jehoiada the priest.
verses.11:10: And the priest gave to the captains of hundreds the spears and the threefold weapons of King David, which were in the house of the Lord.
verses.11:11: And the guards stood, each man with his weapon in his hand, from the right side of the house to the left side of the house, by the altar and the house, all around the king.
verses.11:12: And he brought out the king's son, and put upon him the iezer and the testimony; and he made him king and anointed him, and he clapped with his hand and said, "Long live the king!"
verses.11:13: Now Athaliah heard the sound of the running people, and she came to the people into the house of the Lord.
verses.11:14: And she looked, and behold, the king stood by the pillar according to the ordinance, and the singers and the trumpets were by the king; and all the people of the land were rejoicing and blowing with trumpets. Then Athaliah tore her garments and cried out, "Conspiracy! Conspiracy!"
verses.11:15: And Jehoiada the priest commanded the captains of hundreds, the overseers of the army, and said to them, "Bring them out from within the aseroth, and whoever follows after her shall surely be put to death by the sword." For the priest said, "Do not let her die in the house of the Lord."
verses.11:16: So they laid hands upon her, and they went by the way of the horses' entrance into the king's house, and she died there.
verses.11:17: And Jehoiada made a covenant between the Lord and the king and the people, that they should be a people to the Lord, and also between the king and the people.
verses.11:18: And all the people of the land entered the house of Baal and tore it down; and its altars and its images they broke thoroughly in pieces, and they slew Magthan the priest of Baal before the altars. And the priest appointed overseers over the house of the Lord.
verses.11:19: And he took the captains of hundreds, and the Chorri, and the Rassim, and all the people of the land; and they brought the king down from the house of the Lord, and he entered by the way of the gate of the guards into the king's house, and they seated him upon the throne of the kings.
verses.11:20: And all the people of the land rejoiced, and the city was quiet; and Athaliah they put to death with the sword in the king's house.
verses.12:1: Joash was seven years old when he began to reign.
verses.12:2: In the seventh year of Jehu, Joash began to reign, and he reigned forty years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Abia, from the land of Beersheba.
verses.12:3: And Joash did what was right before the Lord all the days in which Jehoiada the priest instructed him.
verses.12:4: Yet the high places were not removed, and there the people still sacrificed and burned incense on the high places.
verses.12:5: And Joash said to the priests, "All the silver of the holy things that is brought into the house of the Lord, the silver of valuation, the silver a man receives by valuation, and all the silver that comes upon a man's heart to bring into the house of the Lord,
verses.12:6: let the priests take for themselves, each man from his sale, and they themselves shall repair the breach of the house, wherever a breach may be found there."
verses.12:7: And it came to pass in the twenty-third year of King Joash that the priests had not repaired the breach of the house.
verses.12:8: Then King Joash called Jehoiada the priest and the priests, and said to them, "Why have you not been repairing the breach of the house? Now therefore, do not take silver from your sales, for you shall give it for the breach of the house."
verses.12:9: And the priests agreed not to receive silver from the people, and not to strengthen the abomination of the house.
verses.12:10: Then Jehoiada the priest took one chest, and bored a hole in its hole, and placed it beside Iameibein in the house of a man, the house of the Lord; and the priests who guarded the threshold deposited all the silver that was found in the house of the Lord.
verses.12:11: And it came to pass, when he saw that there was much silver in the chest, that the king's scribe and the high priest went up, and bound up and counted the silver that was found in the house of the Lord.
verses.12:12: And he gave the silver that had been prepared into the hands of those who did the work, the overseers of the house of the Lord; and they paid it out to the workers in wood and to the builders who labored in the house of the Lord,
verses.12:13: and to the masons and to the hewers of stone, to buy timber and hewn stones to repair the breach of the house of the Lord, and for all that was expended on the house to strengthen it.
verses.12:14: However, there shall not be made for the house of the Lord silver doors, nails, bowls, and trumpets, nor any vessel of gold or vessel of silver, from the silver that was brought into the house of the Lord;
verses.12:15: for they shall give it to those who do the work. And with it they strengthened the house of the Lord.
verses.12:16: Moreover, they did not require an accounting from the men into whose hands they delivered the silver to give to those who did the work, for they act in their faithfulness.
verses.12:17: The silver for sin and the silver for trespass, whatever was brought into the house of the Lord, belonged to the priests.
verses.12:18: Then Hazael king of Syria went up and fought against Gath, and captured it. And Hazael set his face to go up against Jerusalem.
verses.12:19: So Joash king of Judah took all the holy things that Jehoshaphat, Jehoram, and Ahaziah, his fathers and kings of Judah, had consecrated, and his own holy things, and all the gold that was found in the treasuries of the house of the Lord and of the king's house, and sent them to Hazael king of Syria; and he went up from Jerusalem.
verses.12:20: Now the rest of the acts of Joash, and all that he did, behold, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the days of the kings of Judah?
verses.12:21: And his servants arose and bound every conspiracy, and struck Joash down in the house of Maalo at Gaalla.
verses.12:22: And Jezeichar the son of Jemuath, and Jezebuth, his son Shomer, his servants, struck him, and he died. And they buried him with his fathers in the city of David; and Amaziah his son reigned in his place.
verses.13:1: In the twenty-third year of Joash the son of Ahaziah, king of Judah, Jehoahaz the son of Jehu reigned in Samaria seventeen years.
verses.13:2: And he did what was evil in the sight of the Lord, and walked after the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin; he did not depart from it.
verses.13:3: Then the Lord was moved to wrath against Israel, and He delivered them into the hand of Hazael king of Syria, and into the hand of the son of Hader, the son of Hazael, all those days.
verses.13:4: And Jehoahaz implored the face of the Lord, and the Lord heard him; for He saw the oppression of Israel, because the king of Syria oppressed them.
verses.13:5: And the Lord gave salvation to Israel, and Israel came out from under the hand of Syria; and the children of Israel dwelt in their tents as yesterday and the day before.
verses.13:6: Yet they did not depart from the sins of the house of Jeroboam, who caused Israel to sin, but he walked in it; and moreover the sacred grove remained standing in Samaria.
verses.13:7: For there was not left to Jehoahaz any people except fifty horsemen, ten chariots, and ten thousand footmen; for the king of Syria had destroyed them, and they had made them like dust for trampling.
verses.13:8: Now the rest of the acts of Jehoahaz, and all that he did, and his mighty deeds, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the days of the kings of Israel?
verses.13:9: So Jehoahaz slept with his fathers, and they buried him in Samaria; and Joash his son became king.
verses.13:10: In the thirty-seventh year of Joash king of Judah, Joash the son of Jehoahaz reigned over Israel in Samaria sixteen years.
verses.13:11: And he did what was evil in the sight of the Lord; he did not depart from any sin of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin, but he walked in it.
verses.13:12: Now the rest of the acts of Joash, and all that he did, and his mighty deeds that he performed with Amaziah king of Judah, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the days of the kings of Israel?
verses.13:13: And Joash slept with his fathers, and Jeroboam sat with his fathers and in Samaria with the brethren of Israel.
verses.13:14: Now Elisha fell sick with his illness of which he died; and Joash king of Israel came down to him and wept over his face, and said, "Father, father, the chariot of Israel and its horseman!"
verses.13:15: And Elisha said to him, "Take a bow and arrows." So he took to himself a bow and arrows.
verses.13:16: Then he said to the king, "Place your hand upon the bow." And Joash placed his hand upon it, and Elisha laid his hands upon the king's hands,
verses.13:17: and he said, "Open the window toward the east." And he opened it. And he said, "An arrow of salvation of the Lord, and an arrow of salvation in Syria; and it shall strike Syria in Aphek to utter destruction."
verses.13:18: Then Elisha said to him, "Take bows." And he took them. And he said to the king of Israel, "Strike upon the ground." So the king struck three times, and stopped.
verses.13:19: And the man of God was grieved with him and said, "If you had struck five or six times, then you would have struck Syria to utter destruction; but now you shall strike Syria three times."
verses.13:20: Then Elisha died, and they buried him. And raiding bands of Moab came into the land at the coming of the year.
verses.13:21: And it came to pass, as they were burying a man, behold, they saw the raiding band, and they cast the man into the tomb of Elisha; and he went and touched the bones of Elisha, and he came to life and stood up on his feet.
verses.13:22: And Hazael oppressed Israel all the days of Jehoahaz.
verses.13:23: Yet the Lord had mercy on them and showed compassion to them, and looked upon them because of His covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob; and the Lord was not willing to destroy them, and He did not cast them away from His presence.
verses.13:24: Now Hazael king of Syria died, and the son of Hader, his son, reigned in his place.
verses.13:25: And Joash the son of Jehoahaz turned again and took the cities out of the hand of the son of Hader, the son of Hazael, which he had taken out of the hand of Jehoahaz his father in war. Three times Joash struck him and restored the cities of Israel.
verses.14:1: In the second year of Joash the son of Jehoahaz, king of Israel, Amaziah the son of Joash, king of Judah, began to reign.
verses.14:2: He was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Joadim of Jerusalem.
verses.14:3: And he did what was right in the eyes of the Lord, yet not as David his father; he did according to all that Joash his father had done.
verses.14:4: Only he did not remove the high places; the people still sacrificed and burned incense on the high places.
verses.14:5: Now it came to pass, when the kingdom was established in his hand, that he struck down his servants who had struck down his father.
verses.14:6: Yet he did not put to death the sons of the slayers, as it is written in the book of the laws of Moses, as the Lord commanded, saying, "Fathers shall not die for sons, and sons shall not die for fathers, but rather each shall die in his own sins."
verses.14:7: He struck down ten thousand of Edom in Remele, and he captured the Rock in the battle, and called its name Kathoel, to this day.
verses.14:8: Then Amaziah sent messengers to Joash the son of Jehoahaz, the son of Jehu, king of Israel, saying, "Come, let us look one another in the face."
verses.14:9: And Joash king of Israel sent to Amaziah king of Judah, saying, "The thistle that is in Lebanon sent to the cedar that is in Lebanon, saying, 'Give your daughter to my son as a wife.' And the wild beasts of the field that were in Lebanon passed by and trampled the thistle.
verses.14:10: You have indeed struck down Idumea, and your heart has lifted you up. Glory in this, remaining in your house; and why do you contend in your mischief? You shall fall, both you and Judah with you."
verses.14:11: But Amaziah would not listen. So the king of Israel went up, and he and Amaziah king of Judah looked one another in the face at Beth-shemesh, in the land of Judah.
verses.14:12: And Judah was defeated before Israel, and every man fled to his tent.
verses.14:13: And Joash king of Israel captured Amaziah the son of Joash, the son of Jehoahaz, at Beth-shemesh; and he came to Jerusalem, and broke down four hundred cubits in the wall of Jerusalem, at the Gate of Ephraim even to the Corner Gate.
verses.14:14: And he took the gold and the silver, and all the vessels that were found in the house of the Lord and in the treasuries of the king's house, and the hostages, and returned to Samaria.
verses.14:15: Now the rest of the acts of Joash, all that he did in his might, and how he fought with Amaziah king of Judah, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
verses.14:16: So Joash slept with his fathers, and was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel; and Jeroboam his son reigned in his place.
verses.14:17: And Amaziah the son of Joash, king of Judah, lived fifteen years after the death of Joash the son of Jehoahaz, king of Israel.
verses.14:18: Now the rest of the acts of Amaziah and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
verses.14:19: And they formed a conspiracy against him in Jerusalem, and he fled to Lachish; yet they sent after him to Lachish, and put him to death there.
verses.14:20: And they brought him on horses, and he was buried at Jerusalem with his fathers in the City of David.
verses.14:21: And all the people of Judah took Azariah, who was sixteen years old, and he reigned in place of his father Amaziah.
verses.14:22: He built Elom and restored it to Judah, after the king slept with his fathers.
verses.14:23: In the fifteenth year of Amaziah the son of Joash, king of Judah, Jeroboam the son of Joash reigned over Israel in Samaria forty-one years.
verses.14:24: And he did what was evil before the Lord; he did not depart from all the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin.
verses.14:25: He removed the border of Israel from the entrance of Hamath to the Sea of the Arabah, according to the word of the Lord God of Israel, which He had spoken by the hand of His servant Jonah the son of Amittai, the prophet who was from Gath-chober.
verses.14:26: For the Lord saw the affliction of Israel, that it was exceedingly bitter, and that those who were hemmed in were few, diminished, and forsaken, and there was no helper for Israel.
verses.14:27: And the Lord had not spoken to blot out the seed of Israel from under heaven, and He saved them from the hand of Jeroboam the son of Joash.
verses.14:28: Now the rest of the acts of Jeroboam, and all that he did, and his mighty deeds, how he warred, and how he restored Damascus and Hamath to Judah in Israel, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
verses.14:29: So Jeroboam slept with his fathers, with the kings of Israel; and Azariah the son of Amaziah reigned in place of his father.
verses.15:1: In the twenty-seventh year of Jeroboam king of Israel, Azariah the son of Amaziah, king of Judah, began to reign.
verses.15:2: He was sixteen years old when he began to reign, and he reigned fifty-two years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Chalia of Jerusalem.
verses.15:3: And he did what was right in the eyes of the Lord, according to all that Amaziah his father had done.
verses.15:4: Only he did not remove the high places; the people still sacrificed and burned incense on the high places.
verses.15:5: And the Lord touched the king, so that he was a leper until the day of his death, and he reigned in the house of Apphusoth. And Jonathan the king's son was over the house, judging the people of the land.
verses.15:6: Now the rest of the acts of Azariah, and all that he did, behold, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
verses.15:7: So Azariah slept with his fathers, and they buried him with his fathers in the City of David; and Jonathan his son reigned in his place.
verses.15:8: In the thirty-eighth year of Azariah king of Judah, Zechariah the son of Jeroboam reigned over Israel in Samaria six months.
verses.15:9: And he did what was evil in the eyes of the Lord, as his fathers had done; he did not depart from the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin.
verses.15:10: And Shallum the son of Jabesh conspired against him, and they struck him down at Keblaam and put him to death; and he reigned in his place.
verses.15:11: Now the rest of the acts of Zechariah, behold, they are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.
verses.15:12: This was the word of the Lord which He spoke to Jehu, saying, "Sons of the fourth generation shall sit for you upon the throne of Israel." And so it came to pass.
verses.15:13: And Shallum the son of Jabesh became king; and in the thirty-ninth year of Azariah king of Judah, Shallum reigned for days in Samaria.
verses.15:14: And Menahem the son of Gadi went up from Tharsila and came to Samaria, and struck down Shallum the son of Jabesh in Samaria, and put him to death.
verses.15:15: Now the rest of the acts of Shallum, and the conspiracy which he made, behold, they are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.
verses.15:16: Then Menahem struck even Tirzah, and all who were in it, and its borders from Tirzah, because they did not open to him; so he struck it, and ripped open the women who were with child.
verses.15:17: In the thirty-ninth year of Azariah king of Judah, Menahem the son of Gadi reigned over Israel ten years in Samaria.
verses.15:18: And he did what was evil in the eyes of the Lord; he did not depart from all the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin.
verses.15:19: In his days Phua king of the Assyrians came up against the land; and Menahem gave Phua a thousand talents of silver, that his hand might be with him.
verses.15:20: And Menahem exacted the silver from Israel, from every man mighty in strength, to give to the king of the Assyrians, fifty shekels from each man. So the king of the Assyrians turned back, and did not remain there in the land.
verses.15:21: Now the rest of the acts of Menahem, and all that he did, behold, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
verses.15:22: So Menahem slept with his fathers, and Pekahiah his son reigned in his place.
verses.15:23: In the fiftieth year of Azariah king of Judah, Pekahiah the son of Menahem reigned over Israel in Samaria two years.
verses.15:24: And he did what was evil in the eyes of the Lord; he did not depart from the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin.
verses.15:25: Then Pekah the son of Remaliah, his captain, conspired against him and struck him down in Samaria before the king's house, with Argob and Arieh with him; and with him were fifty men from the four hundred. And he put him to death, and reigned in his place.
verses.15:26: Now the rest of the acts of Pekahiah, and all that he did, behold, they are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.
verses.15:27: In the fifty-second year of Azariah king of Judah, Pekah the son of Remaliah reigned over Israel in Samaria twenty years.
verses.15:28: And he did what was evil in the eyes of the Lord; he did not depart from all the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin.
verses.15:29: In the days of Pekah king of Israel, Algathphellasar king of the Assyrians came and took Ain, and Abel and Thamaacha, and Anioch, and Kenez, and Hazor, and Gilead, and Galilee, all the land of Naphtali; and he carried them captive to the Assyrians.
verses.15:30: And Hoshea the son of Elah formed a conspiracy against Pekah the son of Remaliah, and struck him down and put him to death; and he reigned in his place in the twentieth year of Jotham the son of Ahaz.
verses.15:31: Now the rest of the acts of Pekah, and all that he did, behold, they are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.
verses.15:32: In the second year of Pekah the son of Remaliah, king of Israel, Jonathan the son of Azariah, king of Judah, began to reign.
verses.15:33: He was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Erus, the daughter of Zadok.
verses.15:34: And he did what was right in the eyes of the Lord, according to all that Uzziah his father had done.
verses.15:35: Only he did not remove the high places; the people still sacrificed and burned incense on the high places. He built the Upper Gate of the house of the Lord.
verses.15:36: Now the rest of the acts of Jotham, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
verses.15:37: In those days the Lord began to send out Rezin king of Syria and Pekah the son of Remaliah.
verses.15:38: So Jotham slept with his fathers, and was buried with his fathers in the City of David his father; and Ahaz his son reigned in his place.
verses.16:1: In the seventeenth year of Pekah the son of Remaliah, Ahaz the son of Jotham, king of Judah, began to reign.
verses.16:2: Ahaz was twenty years old when he became king, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem; and he did not do what was upright in the eyes of the Lord God faithfully, like David his father.
verses.16:3: And he walked in the way of the king of Israel; indeed, he even made his son pass through fire, and practiced the abominations of the nations whom the Lord had removed from before the sons of Israel.
verses.16:4: And he sacrificed and burned incense on the high places, and on the hills, and under every leafy tree.
verses.16:5: Then Rezin king of Syria and Pekah the son of Remaliah, king of Israel, went up to Jerusalem to war; and they besieged Ahaz, yet they could not fight.
verses.16:6: At that time Rezin king of Syria restored Elath to Syria, and drove the Jews out of Elath; and the Edomites came to Elath and dwelt there to this day.
verses.16:7: And Ahaz sent messengers to Tiglath-Pileser king of the Assyrians, saying, "I am your servant and your son. Come up, save me from the hand of the king of Syria and from the hand of the king of Israel, who rise up against me."
verses.16:8: And Ahaz took the silver and gold found in the treasuries of the house of the Lord and of the king's house, and sent gifts to the king.
verses.16:9: And the king of the Assyrians heeded him; and the king of the Assyrians went up to Damascus, and captured it and carried it away captive, and put Rezin to death.
verses.16:10: And King Ahaz went to meet Tiglath-Pileser king of the Assyrians at Damascus; and he saw the altar in Damascus. And King Ahaz sent to Uriah the priest the likeness of the altar and its pattern, for all its workmanship.
verses.16:11: And Uriah the priest built the altar according to all that King Ahaz had sent from Damascus.
verses.16:12: And the king saw the altar, and went up upon it,
verses.16:13: and burned his burnt offering and his sacrifice and his drink offering, and poured out the blood of his peace offerings upon the altar,
verses.16:14: the bronze one that was before the Lord; and he brought it forward to the front of the house of the Lord, from between the altar and from between the house of the Lord, and showed it on the side of the altar toward the north.
