verses.16:15: And King Ahaz commanded Uriah the priest, saying, "Upon the great altar offer the morning burnt offering and the evening sacrifice, and the king's burnt offering and his sacrifice, and the burnt offering of all the people and their sacrifice and their drink offering; and all the blood of the burnt offering and all the blood of the sacrifice you shall pour out upon it; and as for the bronze altar, it shall be mine for the morning."
verses.16:16: And Uriah the priest did according to all that King Ahaz had commanded him.
verses.16:17: And the king cut off the side panels of the stands and removed the laver from them; and he took down the sea from the bronze oxen that were beneath it, and placed it upon a stone base.
verses.16:18: And the foundation of the seat he built in the house of the Lord, and the outer entrance of the king he turned toward the house of the Lord because of the king of the Assyrians.
verses.16:19: Now the rest of the acts of Ahaz which he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
verses.16:20: And Ahaz slept with his fathers, and was buried in the City of David; and Hezekiah his son reigned in his place.
verses.17:1: In the twelfth year of Ahaz king of Judah, Hoshea the son of Elah began to reign in Samaria over Israel for nine years.
verses.17:2: And he did what was evil in the eyes of the Lord, yet not as the kings of Israel who were before him.
verses.17:3: Against him came up Shalmaneser king of the Assyrians; and Hoshea became his servant and paid him tribute.
verses.17:4: And the king of the Assyrians found unrighteousness in Hoshea, because he had sent messengers to Segor king of Egypt and had not brought tribute to the king of the Assyrians in that year; therefore the king of the Assyrians besieged him and bound him in a prison house.
verses.17:5: And the king of the Assyrians went up throughout all the land, and went up to Samaria and besieged it for three years.
verses.17:6: In the ninth year of Hoshea, the king of the Assyrians captured Samaria and carried Israel away captive to the Assyrians, and settled them in Halah and in Habor, by the rivers of Gozar, and in the Mountains of the Medes.
verses.17:7: Now it came to pass that the sons of Israel sinned against the Lord their God, who brought them up out of the land of Egypt from under the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt, and they feared other gods,
verses.17:8: and they walked in the statutes of the nations whom the Lord had removed from before the sons of Israel, and the kings of Israel, as many as had made them,
verses.17:9: and as many of the sons of Israel as clothed themselves with words that were not right against the Lord their God; and they built for themselves high places in all their cities, from the tower of the watchmen to the fortified city.
verses.17:10: And they set up for themselves sacred pillars and groves on every high hill and under every leafy tree;
verses.17:11: and they burned incense there on all the high places, just as the nations the Lord had carried away from before them; and they made companions and made engravings to provoke the Lord to anger;
verses.17:12: and they served the idols, of which the Lord had said to them, "You shall not do this thing to the Lord."
verses.17:13: Yet the Lord testified against Israel and against Judah by the hand of all His prophets, every seer of a word: "Turn back from your evil ways, and keep My commandments and My statutes and all the law which I commanded your fathers, all that I sent to them by the hand of My servants the prophets."
verses.17:14: Yet they did not listen, and they stiffened their back more than the back of their fathers;
verses.17:15: and as for His testimonies which He testified to them—they walked after vain things and became vain, and after the nations that were all around them, concerning whom He had commanded them not to do according to these things.
verses.17:16: They forsook the commandments of the Lord their God, and made for themselves a molten image, two heifers, and made groves, and worshiped all the host of heaven and served Baal;
verses.17:17: and they made their sons and their daughters pass through the fire, practiced divination and omens, and sold themselves to do what was evil in the eyes of the Lord, to provoke Him to anger.
verses.17:18: Therefore the Lord was exceedingly angry with Israel, and removed them from His presence; and none was left except the tribe of Judah alone.
verses.17:19: Also Judah did not keep the commandments of God, and they walked in the statutes of Israel which they had made. And they rejected
verses.17:20: the Lord in all the seed of Israel. And He shook them and gave them into the hand of those who plundered them, until He had cast them out from His presence.
verses.17:21: For Israel was apart from the house of David, and they made Jeroboam the son of Nebat king; and Jeroboam drove Israel away from following the Lord and caused them to commit a great sin.
verses.17:22: And the sons of Israel walked in every sin of Jeroboam which he had committed; they did not depart from it,
verses.17:23: until the Lord removed Israel from His presence, just as the Lord had spoken by the hand of all His servants the prophets. And Israel was carried away captive from their own land to the Assyrians, to this day.
verses.17:24: And the king of the Assyrians brought from Babylon, the one from Cuthah, from Aia, and from Hamath and Sepharvaim; and they were settled in the cities of Samaria in place of the sons of Israel; and they inherited Samaria and dwelt in its cities.
verses.17:25: And it came to pass, at the beginning of their dwelling there, that they did not fear the Lord; and the Lord sent lions among them, and they were slaying among them.
verses.17:26: So they spoke to the king of the Assyrians, saying, "The nations whom you have carried away captive and settled in their place in the cities of Samaria do not know the ordinance of the God of the land; therefore He has sent the lions among them, and behold, they are putting them to death, because they do not know the ordinance of the God of the land."
verses.17:27: Then the king of the Assyrians commanded, saying, "Lead away from there, and let them go and dwell there, and they shall enlighten them in the ordinance of the land."
verses.17:28: And they brought one of the priests whom they had carried away captive from Samaria, and he dwelt in Bethel, and he was enlightening them how they should fear the Lord.
verses.17:29: Yet nation by nation they were making their own gods, and put them in the house of the high places which the Samaritans had made, the nations in their cities in which they dwelt;
verses.17:30: and the men of Babylon made Rochchoth-baineithei, and the men of Cuth made Ergel, and the men of Hamath made Ashimath,
verses.17:31: and the Avites made Eblazer and Tartak and Sepharun, when they burned their sons in the fire to Adrammelech and Anammelech of Sepharun.
verses.17:32: And they were fearing the Lord, and settled their abominations in the houses of the high places which they had made in Samaria, nation by nation in the city in which they dwelt; and they were fearing the Lord, and appointed priests of the high places, and they officiated for themselves in the house of the high places.
verses.17:33: The Lord they feared, yet their own gods they served, according to the ordinance of the nations from which he had carried them away captive.
verses.17:34: To this day they have done according to their ordinance; they fear, and they act according to their statutes and according to their judgment, and according to the law and according to the commandment which the Lord commanded the sons of Jacob, whose name He made Israel.
verses.17:35: And the Lord made a covenant with them and commanded them, saying, "You shall not fear other gods nor bow down to them, and you shall not serve them and you shall not sacrifice to them;
verses.17:36: but rather the Lord, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt with great strength and with a high arm—Him you shall fear, and to Him you shall bow down; to Him you shall sacrifice.
verses.17:37: And the statutes, the judgments, the law, and the commandments which He wrote for you, be careful to do all the days; and you shall not fear other gods.
verses.17:38: And the covenant that He has made with you, you shall not forget; and you shall not fear other gods,
verses.17:39: but the Lord your God you shall fear, and He shall deliver you from all your enemies;
verses.17:40: and you shall no longer listen to their ordinance which they practice."
verses.17:41: So these nations feared the Lord, yet served their carved images; indeed, even the sons and the sons of their sons do just as their fathers did, to this day.
verses.18:1: And it came to pass in the third year of Hoshea, son of Elah, king of Israel, that Hezekiah, son of Ahaz, king of Judah, became king.
verses.18:2: He was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem; and the name of his mother was Abu, the daughter of Zechariah.
verses.18:3: And he did what was upright in the eyes of the Lord, according to all that David his father had done.
verses.18:4: He removed the high places, and shattered the pillars, and utterly destroyed the groves and the bronze serpent that Moses had made; for until those days the children of Israel were burning incense to it, and he called it Nesthali.
verses.18:5: He put his hope in the Lord God of Israel, and after him there arose none like him among the kings of Judah, nor among those who were before him;
verses.18:6: and he clung to the Lord; he did not turn away from following Him, and he kept His commandments, all that He had commanded Moses.
verses.18:7: And the Lord was with him, and in all things that he did he acted with understanding; and he rebelled against the king of the Assyrians and did not serve him.
verses.18:8: He struck down the Philistines as far as Gaza and as far as its border, from the tower of the watchmen even to the fortified city.
verses.18:9: And it came to pass in the fourth year of King Hezekiah, which was the seventh year of Hoshea, son of Elah, king of Israel, that Shalmaneser king of the Assyrians came up against Samaria and laid siege against it.
verses.18:10: And he captured it at the end of three years; in the sixth year of Hezekiah, which was the ninth year of Hoshea king of Israel, Samaria was taken.
verses.18:11: And the king of the Assyrians carried Samaria away captive to the Assyrians, and placed them in Halah, and in Habor, the river of Gozan, and in Ore of the Medes,
verses.18:12: because they did not heed the voice of the Lord their God, but transgressed His covenant, even all that Moses the servant of the Lord had commanded; and they did not listen, nor did they do them.
verses.18:13: And in the fourteenth year of King Hezekiah, Sennacherib king of the Assyrians came up against the fortified cities of Judah and captured them.
verses.18:14: And Hezekiah king of Judah sent messengers to the king of the Assyrians at Lachish, saying, "I have sinned; turn away from me. Whatever you lay upon me, I will bear." And the king of the Assyrians imposed upon Hezekiah king of Judah three hundred talents of silver and thirty talents of gold.
verses.18:15: And Hezekiah gave all the silver that was found in the house of the Lord and in the treasuries of the king's house.
verses.18:16: At that time Hezekiah cut off the doors of the temple and the supports that Hezekiah king of Judah had overlaid with gold, and gave them to the king of the Assyrians.
verses.18:17: And the king of the Assyrians sent Thanthan and Raphis and Rabshakeh from Lachish to King Hezekiah with a mighty army against Jerusalem; and they went up and came to Jerusalem, and they stood by the aqueduct of the upper pool, which is on the highway of the fuller's field.
verses.18:18: And they cried out to Hezekiah, and there came to him Eliakim the son of Hilkiah, the steward, and Shebna the scribe, and Jehoshaphat the recorder.
verses.18:19: And Rabshakeh said to them, "Say now to Hezekiah, Thus says the great king, the king of the Assyrians: What is this confidence in which you have trusted?
verses.18:20: You have said—yet they are mere words of the lips—'Counsel and power for war.' Now therefore, in whom have you trusted, that you have rebelled against me?
verses.18:21: Now behold, you have trusted for yourself upon this bruised staff of reed, upon Egypt; if a man leans upon it, it will enter into his hand and pierce it. So is Pharaoh king of Egypt to all who trust in him.
verses.18:22: And since you have said to me, 'We have trusted in the Lord God,' has not this very Hezekiah removed His high places and His altars, and said to Judah and to Jerusalem, 'Before this altar you shall worship in Jerusalem'?
verses.18:23: And now, mingle yourselves with my lord the king of the Assyrians, and I will give you two thousand horses, if you are able on your part to set riders upon them.
verses.18:24: And how will you turn back the face of a single governor among the least of my lord's servants? Yet you have set your hope for yourself on Egypt for chariots and horsemen.
verses.18:25: And now, have we come up without the Lord against this place to destroy it? The Lord said to me, 'Go up against this land and destroy it.'"
verses.18:26: And Eliakim the son of Hilkiah, and Shebna, and Joash said to Rabshakeh, "Speak now to your servants in the Syrian tongue; we understand it, and do not speak with us in the Judean tongue; and why do you speak in the ears of the people who are on the wall?"
verses.18:27: And Rabshakeh said to them, "Has my lord sent me to your lord and to you to speak these words? Is it not to the men sitting upon the wall, that they may eat their own dung and drink their own urine together with you?"
verses.18:28: Then Rabshakeh stood and cried out with a loud voice in the Judean tongue, and he spoke and said, "Hear the words of the great king of the Assyrians.
verses.18:29: Thus says the king: Do not let Hezekiah lift you up with words, for he shall by no means be able to deliver you out of his hand.
verses.18:30: And do not let Hezekiah cause you to hope in the Lord, saying, 'The Lord will surely deliver; this city shall by no means be given into the hand of the king of the Assyrians.'
verses.18:31: Do not listen to Hezekiah, for thus says the king of the Assyrians: Make a blessing with me and come out to me, and each man shall drink of his own vine, and each man shall eat of his own fig tree, and shall drink water from his own cistern,
verses.18:32: until I come and take you to a land like your own land, a land of grain and wine, and of bread and vineyards, a land of oil-bearing olive trees and honey; and you shall live and shall by no means die. And do not listen to Hezekiah, for he deceives you, saying, 'The Lord will rescue you.'
verses.18:33: Have the gods of the nations truly rescued, each one his own land, out of the hand of the king of the Assyrians?
verses.18:34: Where is the god of Hamath and Arphal? Where is the god of Sepharumain? And have they indeed delivered Samaria out of my hand?
verses.18:35: Who among all the gods of the lands are those who have delivered their lands out of my hand, that the Lord should deliver Jerusalem out of my hand?"
verses.18:36: And they kept silent and did not answer him a word, for it was the king's commandment, saying, "You shall not answer him."
verses.18:37: Then Eliakim the son of Hilkiah, the steward, and Shebna the scribe, and Joash the son of Shaphan, the recorder, came in to Hezekiah with their garments torn, and reported to him the words of Rabshakeh.
verses.19:1: And it came to pass, when King Hezekiah heard it, that he tore his garments and covered himself with sackcloth, and entered into the house of the Lord.
verses.19:2: And he sent Eliakim the steward and Somnas the scribe, and the elders of the priests clothed in sackcloth, to Isaiah the prophet, the son of Amoz.
verses.19:3: And he said to him, "Thus says Hezekiah: 'This day is a day of affliction and rebuke and provocation, for children have come to the birth pangs, and there is no strength in her who is giving birth.
verses.19:4: It may be that the Lord your God will hear all the words of Rabshakeh, whom his master, the king of the Assyrians, sent to reproach the living God and to blaspheme with the words that the Lord your God has heard; and you shall lift up a prayer for the remnant that is found.'"
verses.19:5: And the servants of King Hezekiah came to Isaiah.
verses.19:6: And Isaiah said to them, "Thus you shall say to your master: 'Thus says the Lord: Do not be afraid because of the words that you have heard, with which the young servants of the king of the Assyrians have blasphemed.
verses.19:7: Behold, I am putting a spirit in him, and he shall hear a report and return to his own land; and I will strike him down by the sword in his own land.'"
verses.19:8: Then Rabshakeh returned and found the king of the Assyrians warring against Lomna, for he had heard that he had departed from Lachish.
verses.19:9: And he heard concerning Thara king of the Ethiopians, saying, "Behold, he has come out to make war with you." So he returned and sent messengers to Hezekiah, saying,
verses.19:10: "Do not let your God, in whom you trust, delude you, saying, 'Jerusalem shall by no means be delivered into the hands of the king of the Assyrians.'
verses.19:11: Behold, you have heard all that the kings of the Assyrians have done to all the lands, devoting them to destruction; and shall you be delivered?
verses.19:12: Did the gods of the nations deliver them? Did not my fathers destroy both Gozan and Haran, and Rapheis, and the sons of Eden who were in Thaesthen?
verses.19:13: Where is the king of Math and the king of Arpad? And where are Sepharvaim, Anes, and Oudou?"
verses.19:14: And Hezekiah received the letters from the hand of the messengers and read them; and Hezekiah went up to the house of the Lord and spread them out before the Lord.
verses.19:15: And he said, "O Lord, God of Israel, who sit upon the cherubim, You alone are God in all the kingdoms of the earth; You made heaven and earth.
verses.19:16: Incline Your ear, O Lord, and hear; open Your eyes, O Lord, and see; and hear the words of Sennacherib, which he has sent to reproach the living God.
verses.19:17: For truly, O Lord, the kings of the Assyrians have laid waste the nations,
verses.19:18: and have cast their gods into the fire; for they are not gods, but rather the works of men's hands, wood and stone, and they have destroyed them.
verses.19:19: And now, O Lord our God, save us from his hand, and all the kingdoms of the earth shall know that You alone are the Lord God."
verses.19:20: And Isaiah the son of Amoz sent to Hezekiah, saying, "Thus says the Lord, the God of hosts, the God of Israel: 'What you have prayed to Me concerning Sennacherib king of the Assyrians, I have heard.'
verses.19:21: This is the word that the Lord has spoken against him: 'The virgin daughter of Zion has despised you and mocked you; the daughter of Jerusalem has shaken her head at you.
verses.19:22: Whom have you reproached and blasphemed? And against whom have you raised your voice and lifted up your eyes on high? Against the Holy One of Israel.
verses.19:23: By the hand of your messengers you have reproached your Lord, and you have said, "With the multitude of my chariots I will ascend to the height of the mountains, the flanks of Lebanon; and I cut down the stature of its cedar, the choicest of its cypresses; and he came into the midst of the forest and of Carmel.
verses.19:24: I cooled myself and drank foreign waters, and with the sole of my foot I dried up all the rivers of siege."
verses.19:25: I formed it, I gathered it; and it came to be for upheavals from warlike dwellings, fortified cities.
verses.19:26: And those who dwell in them grew weak of hand; they stumbled and were put to shame. They became grass of the field or green herb, grass of the housetops, and a trampling before one who stands.
verses.19:27: And I know your sitting down, and your going out, and your coming in, and your fury against Me.
verses.19:28: Because you have raged against Me, and your insolence has come up into My ears, I will put My hooks in your nostrils and a bridle in your lips, and I will turn you back by the way by which you came.'
verses.19:29: And this shall be the sign to you: Eat this year what grows of itself, and in the second year what springs up; and in the third year there shall be sowing and reaping and planting of vineyards, and you shall eat their fruit.
verses.19:30: And that which has escaped of the house of Judah, that which remains, shall again take root downward and bear fruit upward.
verses.19:31: For out of Jerusalem shall go forth a remnant, and the survivor out of Mount Zion. The zeal of the Lord of hosts shall perform this.
verses.19:32: Not so! Thus says the Lord concerning the king of the Assyrians: 'He shall not enter into this city, nor shoot an arrow there, nor shall a shield come before him, nor shall he pour out a siege mound against it.
verses.19:33: By the way that he came, by it he shall return; and into this city he shall not enter,' says the Lord.
verses.19:34: 'And I will defend this city for My own sake and for the sake of David My servant.'"
verses.19:35: And it came to pass by night that the angel of the Lord went out and struck in the camp of the Assyrians one hundred and eighty-five thousand; and when they rose early in the morning, behold, they were all dead bodies.
verses.19:36: So Sennacherib king of the Assyrians departed and went away and returned, and dwelt in Nineveh.
verses.19:37: And it came to pass, as he was worshiping in the house of Esdrach his god, that Adrammelech and Sharezer his sons struck him down with the sword; and they escaped into the land of Ararat. And Asordan his son reigned in his place.
verses.20:1: In those days Hezekiah became sick to the point of death. And Isaiah the son of Amoz, the prophet, came to him and said to him, "Thus says the Lord: 'Give charge to your house; you are dying, and you shall not live.'"
verses.20:2: Then Hezekiah turned toward the wall and prayed to the Lord, saying,
verses.20:3: "O Lord, I pray, remember now how I have walked before You in truth and with a full heart, and have done Your good in Your sight." And Hezekiah wept with a great weeping.
verses.20:4: And Isaiah was in the middle court, and the word of the Lord came to him, saying,
verses.20:5: "Return and you shall say to Hezekiah, the leader of My people, 'Thus says the Lord, the God of David your father: I have heard your prayer, I have seen your tears; behold, I will heal you. On the third day you shall go up to the house of the Lord.
verses.20:6: And I will add fifteen years to your days, and from the hand of the kings of the Assyrians I will deliver you and this city; and I will defend this city for My own sake and for the sake of David My servant.'"
verses.20:7: And he said, "Let them take a cake of figs and lay it upon the boil, and he shall recover."
verses.20:8: And Hezekiah said to Isaiah, "What is the sign that the Lord will heal me, and that I shall go up to the house of the Lord on the third day?"
verses.20:9: And Isaiah said, "This is the sign from the Lord, that the Lord will perform the word that He has spoken: shall the shadow go forward ten steps, or shall it turn back ten steps?"
verses.20:10: And Hezekiah said, "It is a light thing for the shadow to decline ten steps; no, rather let the shadow turn back on the stairs ten steps backward."
verses.20:11: And Isaiah the prophet cried out to the Lord, and the shadow turned back on the stairs ten steps backward.
verses.20:12: At that time Merodach-Baladan the son of Balaan, king of Babylon, sent letters and a gift to Hezekiah, for he had heard that Hezekiah had been sick.
verses.20:13: And Hezekiah rejoiced over them, and showed them the whole treasure house—the silver and the gold, the spices and the fine oil, and the house of the vessels, and all that was found in his treasuries. There was nothing that Hezekiah did not show them in his house and in all his dominion.
verses.20:14: Then Isaiah the prophet came to King Hezekiah and said to him, "What did these men say, and from where have they come to you?" And Hezekiah said, "They have come to me from a far country, from Babylon."
verses.20:15: And he said, "What have they seen in your house?" And he said, "All that is in my house they have seen; there was nothing in my house that I did not show them, and even the things in my treasuries."
verses.20:16: And Isaiah said to Hezekiah, "Hear the word of the Lord:
verses.20:17: Behold, the days are coming when all that is in your house, and all that your fathers have laid up in store until this day, shall be taken to Babylon; and not a thing shall be left, which the Lord has spoken.
verses.20:18: And your sons who shall go forth from you, whom you shall father, he shall take, and they shall be eunuchs in the house of the king of Babylon."
verses.20:19: And Hezekiah said to Isaiah, "Good is the word of the Lord which He has spoken."
verses.20:20: Now the rest of the acts of Hezekiah, and all his might, and all that he made—the fountain and the aqueduct, and how he brought water into the city—are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the days of the kings of Judah?
verses.20:21: And Hezekiah slept with his fathers, and Manasseh his son reigned in his place.
verses.21:1: Manasseh was twelve years old when he began to reign, and he reigned fifty-five years in Jerusalem, and his mother's name was Hephzibah.
verses.21:2: And he did evil in the sight of the Lord, according to the abominations of the nations whom the Lord had removed from before the sons of Israel.
verses.21:3: And he turned back and built the high places which Hezekiah his father had torn down; and he set up an altar to Baal, and made groves just as Ahab king of Israel had done, and he worshiped all the host of heaven and served them.
verses.21:4: And he built an altar in the house of the Lord, of which He had said, "In Jerusalem I will place My name."
verses.21:5: And he built an altar for all the host of heaven in the two courts of the house of the Lord.
verses.21:6: And he made his sons pass through the fire, and practiced divination and read omens, and appointed a medium and multiplied spiritists, to do evil in the sight of the Lord, to provoke Him to anger.
verses.21:7: And he placed the carved image of the grove in the house of which the Lord had said to David and to Solomon his son, "In this house in Jerusalem I have chosen from all the tribes of Israel, and I will place My name forever,
verses.21:8: and I will not again cause the foot of Israel to be moved from the land which I gave to their fathers, those who will keep all that I have commanded, according to all the commandment which My servant Moses commanded."
verses.21:9: And they did not listen; and Manasseh led them astray to do evil in the sight of the Lord beyond the nations whom the Lord had destroyed from before the sons of Israel.
verses.21:10: And the Lord spoke by the hand of His servants the prophets, saying,
verses.21:11: "Because of all these wicked abominations that Manasseh king of Judah has committed, beyond all that the Amorite before him did, and because he has also caused Judah to sin with their idols,
verses.21:12: not so; thus says the Lord God of Israel: 'Behold, I am bringing calamities upon Jerusalem and upon Judah, so that both ears of everyone who hears shall ring;
verses.21:13: and I will stretch over Jerusalem the measure of Samaria and the plummet of the house of Ahab; and I will wipe Jerusalem clean just as an alabaster jar is wiped clean when it is wiped out and overturned upon its face;
verses.21:14: and I will cast off the remnant of My inheritance, and deliver them into the hands of their enemies, and they shall become a plunder and a spoil to all their enemies,
verses.21:15: because of all the evil he has done in My sight, and they have been provoking Me to anger from the day that I brought their fathers out of Egypt, even until this day.'"
verses.21:16: Moreover, Manasseh also shed very much innocent blood, until he had filled Jerusalem from one end to the other, apart from their sins with which he caused Judah to sin, in doing evil in the sight of the Lord.
verses.21:17: And the rest of the acts of Manasseh, and all that he did, and his sin which he committed, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
verses.21:18: And Manasseh slept with his fathers, and was buried in the garden of his house, in the garden of Uzza; and Amos his son reigned in his place.
verses.21:19: Amos was twenty-two years old when he began to reign, and he reigned two years in Jerusalem, and his mother's name was Meshullam, the daughter of Haruz from Jesebal.
verses.21:20: And he did evil in the sight of the Lord, just as Manasseh his father had done.
verses.21:21: And he walked in every way that his father had walked, and he served the idols which his father had served, and worshiped them.
verses.21:22: And he forsook the Lord God of his fathers, and did not walk in the way of the Lord.
verses.21:23: And the servants of Amos conspired against him, and put the king himself to death in his house.
verses.21:24: And the people of the land struck down all who had conspired against King Amos; and the people of the land made Josiah his son king in his place.
verses.21:25: And the rest of the acts of Amos, all that he did, behold, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
verses.21:26: And they buried him in his tomb in the garden of Uzza; and Josiah his son reigned in his place.
verses.22:1: Josiah was eight years old when he began to reign, and he reigned thirty-one years in Jerusalem, and his mother's name was Jedidah, the daughter of Edina from Basuroth.
verses.22:2: And he did what was right in the sight of the Lord, and walked in every way of David his father; he did not turn aside to the right or to the left.
verses.22:3: And it came to pass in the eighteenth year of King Josiah, in the eighth month, that the king sent Shaphan the son of Eliu, the son of Meshullam, the scribe of the house of the Lord, saying,
verses.22:4: "Go up to Hilkiah the high priest, and seal up the silver that has been brought into the house of the Lord, which those who keep the threshold have gathered from the people,
verses.22:5: and let them place it into the hand of the workmen who are appointed in the house of the Lord." And he gave it to the workmen who were in the house of the Lord, to strengthen the breach of the house,
verses.22:6: to the carpenters and to the builders and to the masons, and to buy timber and hewn stones to reinforce the breach of the house.
verses.22:7: Yet they did not require an accounting from them for the silver given to them, because they act in faithfulness.
verses.22:8: And Hilkiah the high priest said to Shaphan the scribe, "I have found the book of the law in the house of the Lord." And Hilkiah gave the book to Shaphan, and he read it.
verses.22:9: And he came in the house of the Lord to the king, and brought back word to the king, and said, "Your servants have melted down the silver that was found in the house of the Lord, and have delivered it into the hand of the workmen who are appointed in the house of the Lord."
verses.22:10: And Shaphan the scribe spoke to the king, saying, "Hilkiah the priest has given me a book." And Shaphan read it before the king.
verses.22:11: And it came to pass, when the king heard the words of the book of the law, that he tore his garments.
verses.22:12: And the king commanded Hilkiah the priest, and Ahikam the son of Shaphan, and Achbor the son of Micaiah, and Shaphan the scribe, and Asaiah the king's servant, saying,
verses.22:13: "Come and inquire of the Lord for me, and for all the people, and for all Judah, and concerning the words of this book that has been found; for great is the wrath of the Lord that has been poured out upon us, because our fathers did not listen to the words of the book, to do according to all that is written against us."
verses.22:14: So Hilkiah the priest, and Ahikam, and Achbor, and Shaphan, and Asaiah went to Huldah the prophetess, the mother of Shallum the son of Tikvah, the son of Harhas, keeper of the wardrobe; and she dwelt in Jerusalem in the Masena; and they spoke to her.
verses.22:15: And she said, "Thus says the Lord God of Israel: Tell the man who sent you to Me,
verses.22:16: 'Thus says the Lord: Behold, I am bringing calamities upon this place and upon those who dwell in it, all the words of the book which the king of Judah has read,
verses.22:17: because they have forsaken Me and burned incense to other gods, that they might provoke Me to anger with the works of their hands; and My wrath shall be kindled in this place and shall not be quenched.'
verses.22:18: And to the king of Judah, who sent you to inquire of the Lord, thus you shall say to him: 'Thus says the Lord God of Israel: As for the words which you have heard,
verses.22:19: because your heart was tender, and you humbled yourself before the face of the Lord when you heard all that I spoke against this place and against those who dwell in it, that they should become a desolation and a curse, and you tore your garments and wept before Me, I also have heard, says the Lord.
verses.22:20: Not so; behold, I am adding you to your fathers, and you shall be gathered to your tomb in peace, and none of all the calamities which I am bringing upon this place shall be seen by your eyes.'"
verses.23:1: And the kings brought back the word; and the king sent and gathered to himself all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem.
verses.23:2: And the king went up to the house of the Lord, and every man of Judah and those who dwelt in Jerusalem with him, and the priests and the prophets and all the people, from small even to great; and he read before them all the words of the book of the covenant that was found in the house of the Lord.
verses.23:3: And the king stood by the pillar and made a covenant before the Lord, to walk after the Lord, to keep His commandments and His testimonies and His statutes with all his heart and with all his soul, to establish the words of this covenant, the things written in this book; and all the people stood in the covenant.
verses.23:4: And the king commanded Hilkiah the high priest, and the priests of the second order, and those who guarded the threshold, to bring out of the temple of the Lord all the vessels that had been made for Baal, and for the grove, and for all the host of heaven; and he burned them outside Jerusalem in Salemoth of Kidron, and took their dust to Bethel.
verses.23:5: And he burned the Chomarim whom they had given to the king of Judah, and they burned incense on the high places and in the cities of Judah and in the places round about Jerusalem, and those who burned incense to Baal, to the sun, to the moon, to the Mazuroth, and to all the host of heaven.
verses.23:6: And he brought out the grove from the house of the Lord, outside Jerusalem, to the brook Kidron, and burned it at the brook Kidron and ground it to dust, and cast its dust into the grave of the sons of the people.
verses.23:7: And he tore down the house of the Kadesim that were in the house of the Lord, where the women wove Chettiin there for the grove.
verses.23:8: And he brought up all the priests from the cities of Judah, and defiled the high places where the priests had burned incense there, from Gebal even to Beersheba; and he tore down the house of the gates that was by the entrance of the gate of Joshua, the ruler of the gate, which were on a man's left in the gate of the city.
verses.23:9: Nevertheless, the priests of the high places did not come up to the altar of the Lord in Jerusalem, except that they ate unleavened bread in the midst of their brethren.
verses.23:10: And you shall defile Topheth in the valley of the son of Hinnom, for a man to make his son pass through, and a man his daughter, to Molech in fire.
verses.23:11: And he burned the horses that the kings of Judah had given to the sun at the entrance of the house of the Lord, at the treasury of Nathan the king, the eunuch, in Pharurim; and the chariot of the sun he burned with fire.
verses.23:12: And the altars that were on the roof of the upper chamber of Ahaz, which the king of Judah had made, and the altars which Manasseh had made in the two courts of the house of the Lord, the king tore down and pulled down from there, and cast their dust into the brook Kidron.
verses.23:13: And the house that was before Jerusalem, on the right of Mount Mosoath, which Solomon king of Israel had built for Ashtoreth the offense of the Sidonians, and for Chemosh the offense of Moab, and for Molchol the abomination of the sons of Ammon, the king defiled.
verses.23:14: And he broke in pieces the pillars and utterly destroyed the groves, and filled their places with the bones of men.
verses.23:15: Moreover, the high altar that was in Bethel, which Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin, had made—even that high altar he pulled down, and broke its stones in pieces and ground it to dust, and burned the grove.
verses.23:16: And Josiah turned aside and saw the tombs there in the city, and he sent and took the bones out of the tombs and burned them upon the altar, and defiled it according to the word of the Lord which the man of God had spoken when Jeroboam stood at the feast by the altar. And turning around, he lifted up his eyes toward the tomb of the man of God who had spoken these words.
verses.23:17: And he said, "What is that monument which I see?" And the men of the city said to him, "The man of God who came out of Judah and proclaimed these words which he proclaimed against the altar of Bethel."
verses.23:18: And he said, "Leave it alone; let no man move his bones." So his bones were spared together with the bones of the prophet who came from Samaria.
verses.23:19: Moreover, all the houses of the high places that were in the cities of Samaria, which the kings of Israel had made to provoke the Lord to anger, Josiah removed, and did in them all the deeds which he had done in Bethel.
verses.23:20: And he sacrificed all the priests of the high places who were there upon the altars, and burned the bones of men upon them, and returned to Jerusalem.
verses.23:21: And the king commanded all the people, saying, "Keep the Passover to the Lord our God, as it is written in the book of this covenant."
verses.23:22: For this Passover had not been kept from the days of the judges who judged Israel, nor during all the days of the kings of Israel and the kings of Judah,
verses.23:23: but only in the eighteenth year of King Josiah was the Passover kept to the Lord in Jerusalem.
verses.23:24: Moreover, the mediums and the spiritists, and the teraphim and the idols, and all the offenses that were in the land of Judah and in Jerusalem, Josiah put away, that he might establish the words of the law that were written in the book which Hilkiah the priest had found in the house of the Lord.
verses.23:25: Before him there was no king like him who turned to the Lord with all his heart, and with all his strength, and with all his soul, according to all the law of Moses; nor after him did any arise like him.
verses.23:26: Nevertheless, the Lord did not turn from the fierceness of His great wrath, with which His anger burned against Judah, because of the provocations with which Manasseh had provoked Him.
verses.23:27: And the Lord said, "I will also remove Judah from His presence, as I removed Israel, and I will cast off this city which I have chosen, Jerusalem, and the house of which I said, 'My name shall be there.'"
verses.23:28: Now the rest of the acts of Josiah, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
verses.23:29: In his days Pharaoh Necho king of Egypt went up against the king of the Assyrians to the river Euphrates; and Josiah went to meet him. And Necho put him to death at Megiddo when he saw him.
verses.23:30: And his servants carried him dead from Megiddo, and brought him to Jerusalem, and buried him in his own tomb. And the people of the land took Jehoahaz the son of Josiah, and anointed him, and made him king in place of his father.
verses.23:31: Jehoahaz was twenty-three years old when he began to reign, and he reigned three months in Jerusalem; and his mother's name was Hamitai, the daughter of Jeremiah of Lemna.
verses.23:32: And he did what was evil in the sight of the Lord, according to all that his fathers had done.
verses.23:33: And Pharaoh Necho removed him at Ablaa in the land of Hamath, so that he would not reign in Jerusalem, and imposed one hundred talents of silver and one hundred talents of gold.
verses.23:34: And Pharaoh Necho made Eliakim, the son of Josiah king of Judah, reign over them in place of Josiah his father, and changed his name to Jehoiakim. And he took Jehoahaz and brought him into Egypt, and he died there.
verses.23:35: And Jehoiakim gave the silver and the gold to Pharaoh; nevertheless, they taxed the land to give the silver at the command of Pharaoh; each man according to his assessment, they gave the silver and the gold with the people of the land, to give to Pharaoh Necho.
verses.23:36: Jehoiakim was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem; and his mother's name was Jella, the daughter of Edil of Kruma.
verses.23:37: And he did what was evil in the sight of the Lord, according to all that his fathers had done.
verses.24:1: In his days Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up, and Jehoiakim became his servant for three years; then he turned and rebelled against him.
verses.24:2: And he sent against him the raiding bands of the Chaldeans, and the raiding bands of Syria, and the raiding bands of Moab, and the raiding bands of the sons of Ammon, and sent them forth into the land of Judah to prevail, according to the word of the Lord which He spoke by the hand of His servants the prophets.
verses.24:3: Surely because of the wrath of the Lord this came upon Judah, to remove it from His presence, for the sins of Manasseh, according to all that he had done.
verses.24:4: And also he shed innocent blood and filled Jerusalem with innocent blood; and the Lord would not pardon.
verses.24:5: Now the rest of the acts of Jehoiakim, and all that he did, behold, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
verses.24:6: So Jehoiakim slept with his fathers, and Jehoiakim his son reigned in his place.
verses.24:7: And the king of Egypt did not come out of his land anymore, for the king of Babylon had taken all that belonged to the king of Egypt, from the brook of Egypt to the river Euphrates.
verses.24:8: Jehoiakim was eighteen years old when he began to reign, and he reigned three months in Jerusalem; and his mother's name was Nestha, the daughter of Ellanatham of Jerusalem.
verses.24:9: And he did what was evil in the sight of the Lord, according to all that his father had done.
verses.24:10: At that time Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up to Jerusalem, and the city came under siege.
verses.24:11: And Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came into the city, while his servants were besieging it.
verses.24:12: And Jehoiakim king of Judah went out to the king of Babylon, he and his servants and his mother and his princes and his eunuchs; and the king of Babylon took him in the eighth year of his reign.
verses.24:13: And he carried out from there all the treasures of the house of the Lord and the treasures of the king's house, and cut in pieces all the articles of gold which Solomon king of Israel had made in the temple of the Lord, according to the word of the Lord.
verses.24:14: And he carried away into exile Jerusalem, and all the princes and the mighty men of valor, taking ten thousand captives, and every craftsman and smith; and none remained except the poor of the land.
verses.24:15: And he carried Jehoiakim away into exile to Babylon, and the king's mother and the king's wives and his eunuchs; and the mighty men of the land he led away into captivity from Jerusalem to Babylon.
verses.24:16: And all the men of valor, seven thousand, and the craftsmen and the smiths, one thousand, all mighty men who made war—the king of Babylon brought them into exile to Babylon.
verses.24:17: And the king of Babylon made Matthan his son king in his place, and gave him the name Zedekiah.
verses.24:18: Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem; and his mother's name was Mitat, the daughter of Jeremiah.
verses.24:19: And he did what was evil before the Lord, according to all that Jehoiakim had done.
verses.24:20: For it was because of the wrath of the Lord against Jerusalem and in Judah, until He cast them out from His presence. And Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon.
verses.25:1: And it came to pass in the ninth year of his reign, in the tenth month, that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and all his army came against Jerusalem, and he encamped against it and built a siege wall against it all around.
verses.25:2: And the city came under siege until the eleventh year of King Zedekiah, on the ninth day of the month.
verses.25:3: And the famine grew severe in the city, and there was no bread for the people of the land.
verses.25:4: Then the city was breached, and all the men of war went out by night by the way of the gate between the walls, which belongs to the king's garden, while the Chaldeans were against the city all around. And he went by the way of the Arabah.
verses.25:5: And the army of the Chaldeans pursued after the king, and they overtook him in the Araboth of Jericho, and all his army was scattered away from him.
verses.25:6: And they seized the king and brought him to the king of Babylon at Jerdeblatha, and he spoke judgment with him.
verses.25:7: And he slew the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes, and blinded the eyes of Zedekiah; and he bound him in fetters and brought him to Babylon.
verses.25:8: And in the fifth month, on the seventh day of the month, which was the nineteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard, who stood before the king of Babylon, came to Jerusalem.
verses.25:9: And he burned the house of the Lord, and the king's house, and all the houses of Jerusalem, and every house the captain of the guard burned.
verses.25:11: And the remnant of the people who were left in the city, and the deserters who had deserted to the king of Babylon, and the rest of the support, Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard carried away.
verses.25:12: And of the poor of the land the captain of the guard left behind some to be vinedressers and tabein.
verses.25:13: And the bronze pillars that were in the house of the Lord, and the mechonoth, and the bronze sea that was in the house of the Lord, the Chaldeans broke in pieces, and they carried their bronze to Babylon.
verses.25:14: And the cauldrons, and the iamein, and the bowls, and the censers, and all the bronze vessels with which they ministered, he took.
verses.25:15: And the firepans and the golden and silver bowls the captain of the guard took.
verses.25:16: The two pillars, the one sea, and the mechonoth which Solomon had made for the house of the Lord—there was no weighing the bronze of all the vessels.
verses.25:17: Eighteen cubits was the height of the one pillar, and the bronze chothar was upon it; and the height of the chothar was three cubits, with sakacharthai upon the chothar all around, all of bronze; and the second pillar had the same upon the gabacha.
verses.25:18: And the captain of the guard took Seraiah the chief priest, and Zephaniah the son of the second rank, and the three keepers of the threshold.
verses.25:19: And from the city he took one eunuch who was overseer of the men of war, and five men of those who saw the king's face who were found in the city, and the scribe of the commander of the army who mustered the people of the land, and sixty men of the people of the land who were found in the city.
verses.25:20: And Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard took them and led them away to the king of Babylon at Deblatha.
verses.25:21: And the king of Babylon struck them down and put them to death at Riblah in the land of Hamath. Thus Judah was carried away into exile from its own land.
verses.25:22: And as for the people who remained in the land of Judah, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had left, he appointed over them Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan.
verses.25:23: And all the commanders of the army, they and their men, heard that the king of Babylon had appointed Gedaliah; and they came to Gedaliah at Mizpah—even Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, and Jonah the son of Kareth, and Seraiah the son of Tanhumeth the Nepphathite, and Ozonias the son of the Achathite, they and their men.
verses.25:24: And Gedaliah swore to them and to their men, and said to them, "Do not fear the passage of the Chaldeans; dwell in the land and serve the king of Babylon, and it shall be well with you."
verses.25:25: And it came to pass in the seventh month that Manael the son of Nethaniah, the son of Elishama, of the seed of the kings, came, and men with him; and he struck down Gedaliah, and he died, along with the Jews and the Chaldeans who were with him at Mizpah.
verses.25:26: And all the people, from small even to great, and the commanders of the armies arose and entered Egypt, for they were afraid before the face of the Chaldeans.
verses.25:27: And it came to pass in the thirty-seventh year of the captivity of Joakim king of Judah, in the twelfth month, on the twenty-seventh day of the month, that Evil-Merodach king of Babylon, in the year of his reign, lifted up the head of Joakim king of Judah and brought him out of his prison house.
verses.25:28: And he spoke kindly with him, and set his throne above the thrones of the kings who were with him in Babylon.
verses.25:29: And he changed his prison garments, and he ate bread continually before him all the days of his life.
verses.25:30: And his provision was a continual provision; it was given to him from the king's house, a daily portion in its day, all the days of his life.

notes.1:2: Greek reads Baal myian ("Baal-Fly"), translating the Hebrew name Baal-zebub, and adds the closing clause "And they went to inquire through him."
notes.1:3: Greek reads kai ouch houtos ("And it is not so"), a characteristic Septuagint rendering of Hebrew laken ("therefore") as lo ken ("not so"), which recurs in 1:6 and 1:16.
notes.1:18: The Septuagint includes an expanded accession summary of Joram here that differs in several details from 3:1-3, including "his brothers" rather than "his father" and the closing notice of the Lord's wrath against the house of Ahab.
notes.2:1: Greek reads ex Iereicho ("from Jericho") where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "from Gilgal," and adds hos ("as it were") before "into heaven" (also in 2:11).
notes.2:13: Greek reads epanothen Eleisaie ("from upon Elisha"), whereas the Hebrew text reads "from upon him" (referring to Elijah).
notes.2:14: Greek leaves the Hebrew phrase aph-hu ("even he") untranslated as the transliteration appho ("Appho"), incorporating it into Elisha's invocation; the Greek also records Elisha striking the water twice.
notes.2:16: Greek reads heuren ("has found him") and adds "into the Jordan" alongside "upon one of the mountains, or upon one of the hills."
notes.3:4: Greek leaves the Hebrew occupational term noqed ("sheep-breeder") untranslated (rendered here as "noked") and includes the phrase en te epanastasei ("in the rebellion").
notes.3:11: Greek gives Elisha's patronymic as huios Iosaphath ("son of Jehoshaphat"), differing from the Hebrew text's "son of Shaphat."
notes.3:21: Greek reads aneboesan ("they cried out") and adds kai eipon O ("and said, 'Alas!'") before the Moabites take their stand at the border.
notes.3:25: Greek renders tous lithous tou toichou katheremenous ("the stones of the wall torn down"), interpreting as a common noun phrase what appears in the Hebrew text as the place-name Kir-hareseth.
notes.3:27: Greek reads metamelos megas ("great remorse"), expressing regret or revulsion on Israel's part rather than the Hebrew text's "great wrath."
notes.4:2: The Greek reads literally "oil with which I may anoint myself," rendering the underlying Hebrew term for a flask of oil with a verb meaning "anoint."
notes.4:13: The Greek text reads "all this possession" (enktesin), whereas some Greek witnesses read "amazement" or "solicitude" (ekstasin).
notes.4:35: In the Greek text, Elisha himself bows over the child up to seven times before the child opens his eyes, without the sneezing found in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.4:39: "Arioth" is a Greek transliteration of the Hebrew word for wild herbs or greens.
notes.4:42: "Beth-sarisa" preserves the distinct Septuagint place name (corresponding to Hebrew Baal-shalishah), and the Greek renders the accompanying offering as "fig cakes."
notes.5:12: "Apharpha" preserves the distinct Septuagint form of the Damascus river name (corresponding to Hebrew Pharpar).
notes.5:17: The Greek literally reads "a gomer, pairs of mules" (where "gomer" is a transliterated dry measure) and does not include the word "earth" found in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.5:19: "Debratha" is an untranslated Greek transliteration of a Hebrew expression denoting a short stretch of distance.
notes.5:24: The Greek reads "to the dark place," interpreting the Hebrew term for a hill or fortified mound (Ophel) as "darkness."
notes.5:26: The Greek presents Elisha's words as a direct accusation ("And now you have received...") rather than the rhetorical question ("Is it a time to receive...?") of the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.6:5: The Greek reads "hidden" (kekrymmenon), likely an early transcriptional variant for "borrowed" (kechrēmenon, matching the Hebrew).
notes.6:8: "Elimoni" is an untranslated Greek transliteration (elimōni) of the second term in the Hebrew idiom for "such and such."
notes.6:24: "The son of Hader" renders Greek huios Hader, the Septuagint form corresponding to Hebrew Ben-Hadad.
notes.6:25: The Greek reads "fifty" pieces of silver where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "eighty."
notes.6:27: The Greek renders the king's opening exclamation literally as a negative wish ("May the Lord not save you!").
notes.7:1: The Greek mentions only the measure of fine flour in this verse, omitting the two measures of barley that appear later in 7:16 and 7:18.
notes.7:5: The Greek reads "into the midst of" the camp where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "to the edge of" the camp.
notes.7:14: The Greek reads "two riders of horses" sent "after the king of Syria," where the Hebrew reads "two chariots with horses" sent "after the army."
notes.7:17: The Greek reads "when the messenger came down to him" (matching 6:33), where the Hebrew reads "when the king came down to him."
notes.8:7: The Greek renders the royal name Ben-Hadad literally as "son of Hader," reflecting a variant spelling of Hadad; in 8:8–9 "a present" translates the Greek loanword maana (from Hebrew minhah, gift or tribute).
notes.8:10: The Greek verb is second person singular ("you shall surely die"), maintaining direct address rather than shifting to the third person ("he shall surely die").
notes.8:13: The Greek reads "a dead dog" and "reigning over Israel" rather than "over Syria," as found in the Masoretic Hebrew text.
notes.8:17: The Greek gives Joram's reign as forty years rather than eight; in 8:15 "coverlet" renders the Greek transliteration chabba, and 8:21–22 preserve the distinct Greek place names "Seior" and "Senna."
notes.8:28: The Greek reads "king of the foreigners" (allophylon, the usual Septuagint term for Philistines) rather than "king of Syria," and in 8:26 and 8:29 reads "Israel" where the Hebrew has "Jerusalem" (8:26) and "Jezreel" (8:29).
notes.9:7: The Greek uses second person verbs ("you shall avenge" in 9:7 and "you shall utterly destroy" in 9:8) rather than first person; in 9:8 "every male" renders the literal Greek idiom "one who urinates against the wall."
notes.9:10: Here and throughout the chapter (9:15–17, 21, 25, 30, 36–37), the Greek reads "Israel" and "Israelite" where the Hebrew text reads "Jezreel" and "Jezreelite"; in 9:13 "the top of the steps" renders the Greek transliteration garem.
notes.9:16: The Greek preserves an expanded account of Joram's convalescence, specifying his arrow wounds from the Arameans at Ramoth and describing him as "mighty and a man of valor."
notes.9:20: Following the Greek wording faithfully, the watchman reports that the driver was driving Jehu "in a frenzy" rather than comparing the style of driving to Jehu's.
notes.9:27: The Greek preserves the distinct place names "Bethan" and "Gai, which is Ibleam"; in 9:32 the Greek uniquely adds "and saw her" and renders Jehu's words as "Who are you? Come down with me!"
notes.10:6: The Greek reads "Israel" here (and in 10:7, 11) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "Jezreel."
notes.10:10: The Greek reads idete aphpho ("See then"), retaining an untranslated transliteration of the Hebrew particle epho ("then/now") and rendering "see" where the Hebrew has "know."
notes.10:18: The Greek text reads ezelosen ("was zealous for"), differing from the Hebrew "gathered."
notes.10:22: The Greek leaves mesthaal untranslated as a transliteration of the Hebrew term for the wardrobe or vestry.
notes.10:26: The Greek reads stolen ("robe/vestment") rather than stelen ("pillar"), which corresponds to the Hebrew.
notes.11:4: The Greek renders the Hebrew terms for the Carites and the guards as proper-name forms, the Chorri and the Rasin (spelled Rassim in 11:19).
notes.11:8: The Greek transliterates the Hebrew word for "ranks" as aedoth here (and aseroth in 11:15, where it also uses the plural "them" before "after her"), and concludes with a third-person past verb ("And he was") rather than a plural command.
notes.11:9: The Greek calls Jehoiada ho synetos ("the wise/discerning") here, whereas the Hebrew reads "the priest."
notes.11:12: The Greek transliterates the Hebrew word for "crown/diadem" as iezer, and reads ekratesen (a manuscript spelling reflecting ekrotesen, "clapped") in the singular.
notes.11:18: The Greek spells the name of Baal's priest Magthan, corresponding to Hebrew Mattan.
notes.12:2: The Greek names Joash's mother Abia and adds "from the land of Beersheba," where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "Zibiah of Beersheba."
notes.12:6: "Sale" translates Greek prasis (likewise "sales" in v. 8), where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "acquaintance"; "breach" translates the Greek transliterated loanword bedek, also used in vv. 7, 8, and 13.
notes.12:9: The Greek reads bdelygma ("abomination") here instead of the transliterated loanword bedek ("breach") found in vv. 6-8 and 13.
notes.12:10: The Greek literally reads "bored a hole in its hole" and places the chest "beside Iameibein in the house of a man, the house of the Lord," retaining an untranslated term (Iameibein) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text refers to the right side of the altar as one enters the house of the Lord.
notes.12:22: The Greek gives distinct forms for the conspirators' names ("Jezeichar the son of Jemuath, and Jezebuth") and reads "his son Shomer," where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "Jozacar son of Shimeath and Jehozabad son of Shomer."
notes.13:3: "The son of Hader" translates Greek huios Hader (likewise in vv. 24-25), the Septuagint rendering of the Syrian royal name Ben-Hadad.
notes.13:13: The Greek reads "and Jeroboam sat with his fathers and in Samaria with the brethren of Israel," differing from the Hebrew Masoretic Text, which states that Jeroboam sat on his throne and Joash was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel.
notes.13:17: The Greek omits Elisha's command to shoot and Joash's shooting of the arrow, and uses a third-person future verb ("it shall strike") referring to the arrow where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "you shall strike."
notes.13:18: "Bows" translates Greek plural toxa (which can denote archery gear generally), where the Hebrew Masoretic Text specifies "arrows."
notes.14:7: The Greek reads Remele (an early corruption of 'Valley of Salt') and Kathoel (corresponding to Hebrew Joktheel).
notes.14:13: The Greek text names Amaziah's grandfather as Jehoahaz, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads Ahaziah.
notes.14:25: The Greek verb literally reads 'removed' (probably a textual shortening of 'restored'), and spells Jonah's hometown Gath-chober (Hebrew Gath-hepher).
notes.14:27: The Greek reads 'the seed of Israel' (Hebrew 'name') and 'from the hand of Jeroboam' (Hebrew 'by the hand of Jeroboam').
notes.14:29: The Greek text here reads 'Azariah the son of Amaziah' rather than Jeroboam's son Zechariah (cf. 15:8), an early scribal anticipation of 15:1.
notes.15:5: The Greek reads 'reigned' (Hebrew 'dwelt'), transliterates the Hebrew term for a separate house of isolation as 'Apphusoth', and names the king's son Jonathan (as also in 15:7, 32; cf. Jotham in 15:30, 36, 38).
notes.15:10: The Greek transliterates the Hebrew phrase 'before the people' as a place name, Keblaam, and uses plural verbs for the conspirators' attack.
notes.15:16: The Greek reads 'Tirzah' in both places, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text has Menahem attacking Tiphsah from Tirzah.
notes.15:19: The Greek names the Assyrian king Phua (Hebrew Pul); similarly in 15:29 the Greek reads Algathphellasar (Hebrew Tiglath-pileser) along with the distinct town names Ain, Abel and Thamaacha, Anioch, and Kenez.
notes.15:25: The Greek reads 'fifty men from the four hundred' (Hebrew 'of the Gileadites'); in 15:30 the Greek also reads 'Jotham the son of Ahaz' (Hebrew 'Uzziah').
notes.16:14: The Greek links 'the bronze one that was before the Lord' directly to 'the altar' in verse 13 and reads 'showed it' (Greek edeixen) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has 'put it.'
notes.16:15: The Greek renders the final phrase 'for the morning' (Greek eis to proi), reflecting a different vocalization of the Hebrew consonants than the Masoretic Text's 'to inquire by.'
notes.16:17: The Greek transliterates the Hebrew term for the wheeled temple stands as mechonoth.
notes.16:18: The Greek reads 'the foundation of the seat he built' and 'turned toward the house of the Lord,' whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text refers to the Sabbath canopy that they had built and to removing the outer entrance.
notes.17:4: The Greek names the Egyptian king 'Segor' (Hebrew Masoretic Text: 'So'), transliterates the Hebrew term for tribute as manaa (also manach in verse 3), and reads 'in that year' and 'besieged him.'
notes.17:6: The Greek reads 'rivers of Gozar' and 'Mountains of the Medes,' where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has 'river of Gozan' and 'cities of the Medes.'
notes.17:20: In the Greek text, the sentence begins at the end of verse 19 with a plural verb making Israel the subject ('And they rejected the Lord in all the seed of Israel'), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text has the Lord rejecting Israel.
notes.17:30: The Greek preserves distinct deity names in verses 30–31—Rochchoth-baineithei (Hebrew: Succoth-Benoth), Ergel (Hebrew: Nergal), Ashimath (Hebrew: Ashima), and Eblazer (Hebrew: Nibhaz)—and treats Sepharun (Hebrew: the Sepharvites) as an idol made by the Avites.
notes.17:34: Unlike the Hebrew Masoretic Text, the Greek omits the negation here ('they fear, and they act according to their statutes...'), and in verse 40 uses a second-person future ('you shall no longer listen') continuing the Lord's speech from verses 35–39.
notes.18:2: The Greek text gives the name of Hezekiah's mother as Abu (Abou), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads Abi.
notes.18:4: The Greek text calls the bronze serpent Nesthali (where the Hebrew reads Nehushtan), renders the Asherah poles as groves, and places both the groves and the serpent under the single verb utterly destroyed.
notes.18:11: The Greek states that the king carried away Samaria (rather than Israel) and reads Ore of the Medes, a proper name or reading of mountains where the Hebrew reads cities of the Medes.
notes.18:17: The Greek renders the first two Assyrian official titles as Thanthan and Raphis, where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads Tartan and Rabsaris.
notes.18:18: The Greek identifies the recorder here as Jehoshaphat, and later as Joash (v. 26) and Joash the son of Shaphan (v. 37), where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads Joah the son of Asaph.
notes.18:23: Mingle yourselves follows the Greek verb michthete, reflecting a Septuagint rendering of the Hebrew root for associate or mingle rather than give pledges or make a wager.
notes.18:34: The Greek has singular god in both questions, gives the place names as Arphal and Sepharumain (for Hebrew Arpad and Sepharvaim), and does not include Hena and Ivvah.
notes.19:2: The Greek text uses the distinct name form Somnas (Heb. Shebna), and similarly preserves distinctive Septuagint name forms throughout the chapter: Lomna (v. 8), Thara (v. 9), Rapheis and Thaesthen (v. 12), Math, Anes, and Oudou (v. 13), and Esdrach and Asordan (v. 37).
notes.19:23: The Greek reads "your Lord" (with the possessive pronoun) and shifts to the third person ("he came into the midst of the forest and of Carmel"); in v. 24, "I cooled myself" reflects a reading of the Hebrew root as "be cool" rather than "dig."
notes.19:25: The Septuagint here is markedly shorter and differently phrased than the Hebrew Masoretic Text, omitting the opening question ("Have you not heard...") and reading "for upheavals from warlike dwellings, fortified cities."
notes.19:32: The Greek reads "Not so!" (ouch houtos), taking the Hebrew consonants lkn as "not so" rather than "therefore."
notes.20:4: The Greek states simply that "Isaiah was in the middle court," differing from the Hebrew Masoretic Text ("before Isaiah had gone out of the middle court").
notes.20:12: The Greek gives the father's name as Balaan (Heb. Baladan) and transliterates Hebrew terms here ("a gift," Gk. manaan) and in v. 13 ("the treasure house," Gk. oikon tou nechotha).
notes.20:17: The Greek renders "and not a thing shall be left, which the Lord has spoken," connecting the closing attribution to "thing" (rhema) with a relative pronoun rather than as an independent clause ("says the Lord").
notes.20:19: The Septuagint ends the verse here, omitting Hezekiah's additional reflection found in the Hebrew Masoretic Text ("Will there not be peace and truth in my days?").
notes.21:6: The Greek reads plural "his sons" (Hebrew: "his son") and contains the difficult reading ἐλλήν (here rendered "a medium"), a manuscript variant for θελητήν used in the Septuagint for a necromancer or medium.
notes.21:12: "Not so" faithfully translates Greek οὐχ οὕτως, a characteristic kaige-Septuagint rendering of the Hebrew word for "therefore" (laken), also seen in 22:20.
notes.21:13: The Greek uses the vivid image of an alabaster jar (ἀλάβαστρος) wiped clean and overturned, where the Hebrew text speaks of a dish or bowl.
notes.21:18: Here and throughout verses 19-25 the Greek consistently names Manasseh's son Amos (Ἀμώς) rather than Hebrew Amon; similarly, verse 19 preserves the distinct Greek forms Meshullam and Jesebal (Hebrew: Meshullemeth and Jotbah).
notes.22:1: The Greek preserves the distinct proper names Edina and Basuroth (Hebrew: Adaiah and Bozkath).
notes.22:3: The Greek specifies "in the eighth month" (absent from the Hebrew), names Shaphan's father Eliu (Hebrew: Azaliah), and reads "the scribe of the house of the Lord" without a preposition before "house."
notes.22:5: "Breach" renders Greek βέδεκ (also in 22:6), a direct transliteration of the Hebrew term for structural damage; the Greek also shifts from Josiah's command to past-tense narration with "And he gave it."
notes.22:14: The Greek explicitly identifies Huldah as "the mother of Shallum" (Hebrew: "the wife of Shallum") and transliterates the Jerusalem district as "the Masena" (μασενά, Hebrew for the Second Quarter).
notes.22:20: As in 21:12, "Not so" translates Greek οὐχ οὕτως (for Hebrew "therefore"); the Greek chapter also ends at "this place," omitting the closing Hebrew sentence about the messengers returning word to the king.
notes.23:1: The Greek opens with "the kings brought back the word," whereas the Hebrew closes 22:20 with "they brought back word to the king."
notes.23:5: The Greek reads "burned" (Hebrew "removed") and retains Hebrew terms in transliteration as "Chomarim" (idolatrous priests) and "Mazuroth" (constellations); similar Greek transliterations or forms appear in v. 4 ("Salemoth"), v. 7 ("Kadesim," "Chettiin"), v. 8 ("Gebal"), and v. 11 ("Pharurim").
notes.23:10: The Greek reads second-person plural "you shall defile" and lacks the negative particle before the infinitive, whereas the Hebrew reads "he defiled ... so that no one might make his son or daughter pass through the fire."
notes.23:13: The Greek reads "the house" (Hebrew "the high places") and preserves the distinct forms "Mosoath" (Hebrew "Destruction") and "Molchol" (Hebrew "Milcom").
notes.23:33: The Greek reads "removed him at Ablaa" (Hebrew "imprisoned him at Riblah") and has "one hundred talents of gold" (Hebrew "one talent of gold"); vv. 31 and 36 also preserve distinct Greek name forms (Hamitai, Lemna, Jella, Edil, Kruma).
notes.24:2: The Greek omits "the Lord" as the explicit subject of "sent" (present in the Hebrew) and reads "to prevail" where the Hebrew has "to destroy it."
notes.24:6: Here and in vv. 8, 12, and 15 the Greek names the son "Jehoiakim," identical to his father, whereas the Hebrew distinguishes him as "Jehoiachin" (v. 8 also preserves the Greek name forms Nestha and Ellanatham).
notes.24:17: The Greek calls the new king "Matthan his son," whereas the Hebrew reads "Mattaniah his uncle"; v. 18 likewise preserves the Greek name "Mitat" (Hebrew "Hamutal") and omits "of Libnah."
notes.25:6: Jerdeblatha (and Deblatha in v. 20) are distinct Septuagint forms of Riblah (v. 21). In v. 8, the title rendered "captain of the guard" is Greek archimageiros (literally "chief cook"), the Septuagint rendering of the Babylonian court office over the royal guard.
notes.25:17: In vv. 12-17 the Greek text retains several untranslated transliterations of Hebrew technical terms: tabein (plowmen), mechonoth (wheeled stands), iamein (shovels), chothar (capital), sakacharthai (latticework and pomegranates), and gabacha (network).
notes.25:18: The Greek reads "son of the second rank" (hyion tes deuteroseos), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "the second priest."
notes.25:23: The Septuagint preserves distinctive proper-name forms here ("Jonah the son of Kareth," "the Nepphathite," and "Ozonias the son of the Achathite"), as well as "Manael" in v. 25 (for Ishmael) and "Joakim" in v. 27 (corresponding to Jehoiachin).
notes.25:24: The Greek reads "the passage of the Chaldeans" (parodon), differing from the Masoretic Text's "servants of the Chaldeans."
